Many people uphold the stance that 95% of DNA is junk.

standard.definition:
n. a basis for comparison; a reference point against which other things can be evaluated
n. a board measure = 1980 board feet
n. the value behind the money in a monetary system
n. an upright pole or beam (especially one used as a support)
standard.translation: n. 标准, 规格, 旗, 军旗, 本位\na. 标准的, 合规格的\n[计] 标准

examples.en: Standard Chinese, commonly referred to as Mandarin, is based on Pekinese.
examples.zh: 中文的标准语，也就是人们常说的普通话，以北京口音为基础。

examples.en: We tried to come up to the standard.
examples.zh: 我们尝试达到标准。

examples.en: Our company will implement new price standards regarding this product.
examples.zh: 关于这个产品，我公司将执行新的价格标准。

standpoint.definition: n a mental position from which things are viewed

examples.en: We can consider the problem from several standpoints.
examples.zh: 我们可以从几个观点来考虑这个问题。

standstill.definition: n a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible\nn an interruption of normal activity
standstill.translation: n. 停止, 停顿\n[医] 停顿

examples.en: Traffic in the city centre has come to a standstill.
Their business came to a standstill for want of money.
My business is at a standstill because of the recession.

staple.definition:
n. a natural fiber (raw cotton, wool, hemp, flax) that can be twisted to form yarn
n. a short U-shaped wire nail for securing cables
n. paper fastener consisting of a short length of U-shaped wire that can fasten papers together
v. secure or fasten with a staple or staples
staple.translation: n. 主要产物, 常用品, 主要要素, 原料, 订书钉, 钩环\na. 主要的, 重要的\nvt. 分级, 钉住

examples.en: In China, southern people eat rice as staple food; northern people eat wheaten food as staple food.
examples.zh: 在中国，南方人以米饭为主食，北方人以面食为主食。

stare.definition: n. a fixed look with eyes open wide\nv. fixate one's eyes
stare.translation: vi. 注视, 凝视, 瞪视, 显眼\nvt. 盯\nn. 凝视

examples.en: It's embarrassing to be seen without make-up so please don't stare.
examples.zh: 素颜太害羞了，请不要盯着我看。

examples.en: My manager stared at me as if he was angry.
examples.zh: 经理像是生气了一样盯着我。

examples.en: It is rude to stare at someone.
examples.zh: 盯著别人看是不礼貌的。

start.definition:
n. the beginning of anything
n. a turn to be a starter (in a game at the beginning)
n. a line indicating the location of the start of a race or a game
n. the advantage gained by beginning early (as in a race)
start.translation:
n. 惊起, 出发, 开端, 起点, 吃惊, 有利条件
vi. 开始, 出发, 启动, 跳起, 吃惊, 出现, 松动, 脱落, 起价, 参赛
vt. 使惊起, 开动, 发动, 启动, 开始, 创办, 提议, 使松动, 使脱落, 起用
[计] 起始

examples.en: The World Cup is going to start on the 11th.
examples.zh: 世界杯 11 号就要开始了。

examples.en: We were about to start, when it began to rain.
examples.zh: 我们刚要开始，这时天空下起了雨。

examples.en: When I speak Chinese, I start to feel at ease.
examples.zh: 我说中文的时候，开始感到自在了。

startle.definition: n. a sudden involuntary movement\nv. to stimulate to action\nv. move or jump suddenly, as if in surprise or alarm
startle.translation: n. 惊愕, 惊恐\nvt. 吃惊, 使惊愕\nvi. 惊起

examples.en: Avoid sudden movements around the rabbit, they can startle them.
examples.zh: 避免在兔子旁边突然做出动作，以免吓到牠们。

examples.en: Tom looked a little startled.
examples.zh: 汤姆看起来有点惊讶。

starvation.definition: n. a state of extreme hunger resulting from lack of essential nutrients over a prolonged period\nn. the act of depriving of food or subjecting to famine
starvation.translation: n. 饥饿, 饿死\n[医] 绝食, 饥锇(指长时期的)

examples.en: The survivors were found on an island, dying of starvation.
examples.zh: 幸存者在一个岛上被找到了，已经饿得要死了。

examples.en: The poor child was on the verge of starvation.
examples.zh: 那可怜的孩子快饿死了。

examples.en: Many children die of starvation in Africa.
examples.zh: 在非洲有许多孩子死于饥饿。

starve.definition:
v. be hungry; go without food
v. die of food deprivation
v. deprive of food
v. deprive of a necessity and cause suffering

examples.en: Millions of people starve to death every year.
examples.zh: 每年有几百万人死于饥饿。

examples.en: A lot of people are starving in the world.
examples.zh: 世界上许多人很饥饿。

examples.en: We should all help provide starving people with food.
examples.zh: 我们应该尽可能的帮忙提供食物给饥饿中的人们.

state.definition:
n. the territory occupied by one of the constituent administrative districts of a nation
n. the way something is with respect to its main attributes
n. the group of people comprising the government of a sovereign state
n. a politically organized body of people under a single government
state.translation:
n. 州, 状态, 情形, 国家, 政府, 领土, 国务, 社会地位
a. 国家的, 正式的, 礼仪用的, 州的
vt. 说明, 陈述, 规定
[计] 状态

examples.en: Some analysts consider Somalia as the failed state par excellence.
examples.zh: 一些分析家认为索马里是非常失败的国家。

examples.en: Federal, state, and community officials immediately pledged to rebuild it.
examples.zh: 联邦、州及地方官员立即承诺将其重建。

examples.en: The patient is in a state of profound stupor.
examples.zh: 患者现在处于深度昏迷状态。

statement.definition:
n. a message that is stated or declared; a communication (oral or written) setting forth particulars or facts etc
n. (music) the presentation of a musical theme
n. a nonverbal message
n. a document showing credits and debits
statement.translation: n. 陈述, 指令, 声明\n[计] 程序语句; 语句

examples.en: I began to doubt the accuracy of his statement.
examples.zh: 我开始怀疑他陈述的准确性。

examples.en: To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
examples.zh: 要你在多大程度上同意或不同意这种说法？

examples.en: The family was highly doubtful of the statement from the military.
examples.zh: 家属对军方的说法高度置疑。

statesman.definition: n. a man who is a respected leader in national or international affairs

examples.en: The boy grew up to be a great statesman.
examples.zh: 这个孩子长大后成为了一个伟大的政治家。

examples.en: The name of this statesman is known to everybody in Japan.
examples.zh: 这位政治家的名字在日本人人皆知。

examples.en: He is the greatest statesman that ever lived.
examples.zh: 他是古今无匹的伟大政治家。

stationary.definition: s. standing still\ns. not capable of being moved
stationary.translation: a. 不动的, 静止的, 不变的, 固定的, 停留的\n[计] 定常, 定态, 固定的

examples.en: The albatross appeared to be stationary in the air.
There was a stationary lorry in the middle of the road.
Ziri jumped out of the stationary vehicle and began to flee.

statistical.definition: a. of or relating to statistics
statistical.translation: a. 统计的, 统计上的, 统计学的\n[经] 统计的, 统计学的

examples.en: In this semester, students study and apply statistical sampling techniques.
Benedito's research involves analyzing complex data sets using statistical methods.
Yanni found this in a statistical yearbook of Algeria.

statistics.definition: n. a branch of applied mathematics concerned with the collection and interpretation of quantitative data and the use of probability theory to estimate population parameters
statistics.translation: n. 统计学, 统计资料\n[计] 统计信息

examples.en: The aviation expert analyzed the statistics in detail.
examples.zh: 航空专家详细分析了统计数据。

examples.en: Facts are stubborn things, but statistics are pliable.
examples.zh: 事实是倔强的，但统计是柔顺的。

statue.definition: n. a sculpture representing a human or animal
statue.translation: vt. 以雕像装饰\nn. 雕像

examples.en: Their wish is engraved on the base of the statue.
examples.zh: 他们的愿望被刻在雕像的底座上。

examples.en: The statue was carved from a block of cherry wood.
examples.zh: 这座雕像是由樱木雕刻而成。

examples.en: This statue is as large as life.
examples.zh: 这座雕像和真人的尺寸一样。

status.definition: n. the relative position or standing of things or especially persons in a society
status.translation: n. 状态, 情形, 地位, 要人身份\n[计] 状态

examples.en: Obviously, they are jealous of his wealth and status.
examples.zh: 他们很明显在嫉妒他的财富和地位。

examples.en: I believe that a fine education can change one's social status.
examples.zh: 我相信良好的教育能改变人的社会地位。

examples.en: Can you tell me about your marital status?
examples.zh: 能告诉我你的婚姻状况吗？

statute.definition: n an act passed by a legislative body\ns enacted by a legislative body
statute.translation: n. 法令, 成文法律, 法规, 章程, 条例\n[法] 法令, 法规, 成文法

examples.en: The statute of limitations has already passed for this crime.
He got off because of the statute of limitations.
The statute of limitations for this case has expired.

stay.definition:
n. continuing or remaining in a place or state
n. a judicial order forbidding some action until an event occurs or the order is lifted
n. a thin strip of metal or bone that is used to stiffen a garment (e.g. a corset)
n. (nautical) brace consisting of a heavy rope or wire cable used as a support for a mast or spar
stay.translation: n. 停留, 逗留, 制止, 延缓, 停止, 支柱, 支撑物, 支索\nvt. 制止, 延缓, 坚持, 支持, 支撑, 用支索固定\nvi. 停留, 逗留, 暂停, 坚持, 中止

examples.en: I want you to stay here until I get back.
examples.zh: 我想你待在这里直到我回来。

examples.en: You can stay here as long as you want to.
examples.zh: 你愿意在这里呆多久就呆多久。

examples.en: I want to stay here for a couple of days.
examples.zh: 我想在这儿待几天。

steady.definition:
v. make steady
a. not subject to change or variation especially in behavior
s. securely in position; not shaky
s. not easily excited or upset
steady.translation: a. 稳定的, 不动摇的, 沉着的, 稳固的, 坚定的, 经常的\nvt. 使稳定, 使坚定\nvi. 变为沉着, 稳固

examples.en: He was walking up the hill at a steady pace.
examples.zh: 他迈着稳健的步伐登上了山丘。

examples.en: The immigrants entered the country in a steady flow.
examples.zh: 移民川流不息地进入这个国家。

examples.en: There was a steady increase in population.
examples.zh: 人口稳定地增加。

steam.definition:
n. water at boiling temperature diffused in the atmosphere
v. emit steam
v. rise as vapor
v. get very angry
steam.translation:
n. 蒸汽, 精力
a. 蒸汽的
vi. 蒸发, 行驶, 发怒
vt. 蒸, 煮, 散发

examples.en: Do you know if there's a steam room anywhere around here?
examples.zh: 你知道这附近哪里有汗蒸房吗？

examples.en: Water turns into steam when it is boiled.
examples.zh: 水沸腾后变为蒸汽。

examples.en: Is there a difference between steamed buns and steamed bread?
examples.zh: 馒头和馍馍有区别吗？

steel.definition:
n. an alloy of iron with small amounts of carbon; widely used in construction; mechanical properties can be varied over a wide range
n. knife sharpener consisting of a ridged steel rod
v. get ready for something difficult or unpleasant
v. cover, plate, or edge with steel
steel.translation: n. 钢, 钢制品, 钢铁, 坚硬, 坚固\na. 钢的, 钢制的, 钢铁业的, 坚强的\nvt. 使坚强, 钢化, 使冷酷

examples.en: Steel production will increase 2% this month from last month.
examples.zh: 今个月的钢铁产量和上个月比起来，估计会上升两个巴仙。

examples.en: There are daisies next to the steel building.
examples.zh: 在钢铁大厦的旁边有许多的雏菊。

examples.en: According to an estimate, steel production will reach 100 million tons this year.
examples.zh: 一项估计显示，今年的钢鉄产量将会达到一亿吨。

steep.definition:
n. a steep place (as on a hill)
v. devote (oneself) fully to
v. let sit in a liquid to extract a flavor or to cleanse
a. having a sharp inclination
steep.translation: n. 浸渍, 悬崖\na. 险峻的, 陡峭的, 急剧升降的, 夸大的\nv. 浸, 泡

examples.en: The path zigzagged up the steep slope.
examples.zh: 这条小路沿著陡峭的斜坡蜿蜒而上。

examples.en: My cousin is so steeped in schoolwork that his friends call him bookworm.
examples.zh: 我的表兄弟太过沉浸于学业，以致于他的朋友们唤他作书虫。

steer.definition: v. direct the course; determine the direction of travelling\nv. direct (oneself) somewhere
steer.translation: vt. 引导, 驾驶, 航行, 控制\nvi. 驾驶, 掌舵, 行驶\nn. 驾驶指示, 劝告

examples.en: Japanese cars' steering wheels are on the right.
examples.zh: 日本车的方向盘在右边。

stem.definition:
n. the tube of a tobacco pipe
v. grow out of, have roots in, originate in
v. cause to point inward
v. stop the flow of a liquid
stem.translation: n. 茎, 干, 柄, 船首, 血统, 堵塞物\nvt. 摘掉茎, 装柄于, 阻止, 堵住, 逆行\nvi. 堵住, 逆行

examples.en: From what stems this contradiction between our hopes and our reality?
examples.zh: 希望与现实之间的矛盾，因何而起？

examples.en: Their trouble stems from a trifling matter.
examples.zh: 他们的烦恼是由一件琐碎的事而起的。

step.definition:
n. the act of changing location by raising the foot and setting it down
n. support consisting of a place to rest the foot while ascending or descending a stairway
n. a short distance
n. a solid block joined to the beams in which the heel of a ship's mast or capstan is fixed
step.translation:
n. 步骤, 步, 步幅, 脚步声, 踏级, 步伐, 短距离, 步态, 手段, 等级
vt. 踏, 以步测量, 跨步, 使成阶梯状
vi. 跨步, 轻快地走, 跳舞, 踩, 踏上, 行走
[计] 步骤

examples.en: A single step, and you will fall over the cliff.
examples.zh: 只迈一步，你就会落下悬崖。

examples.en: Maybe we should take a step back before we fall?
examples.zh: 我们是不是该退一步，免得倒下？

examples.en: Another step, and you would have fallen down the stairs.
examples.zh: 再走一步的话，你就已经跌下楼梯了。

stereo.definition: n. reproducer in which two microphones feed two or more loudspeakers to give a three-dimensional effect to the sound\nn. two photographs taken from slightly different angles that appear three-dimensional when viewed together
stereo.translation: n. 铅版, 立体照片\na. 立体的, 立体感觉的

examples.en: Put a record on the stereo.
examples.zh: 往立体声音响上放一枚唱片。

stereotype.definition: n. a conventional or formulaic conception or image
stereotype.translation: n. 铅版, 陈规, 老套\nvt. 使用铅版, 把...印制成盲文, 套用老套, 使一成不变

examples.en: It is a stereotype that police officers always eat doughnuts.
examples.zh: 警察总吃甜甜圈是一种刻板印象。

examples.en: This film attempts to break stereotypes and redefine what true masculinity is.
examples.zh: 这部电影试图打破刻板印象，重新诠释何谓真正的男性特质。

examples.en: The stage charisma of drag performers compels audiences to reconsider their own stereotypes.
examples.zh: 反串秀者的舞台魅力使观众不禁重新审视自己的刻板印象。

sterling.definition: n. British money; especially the pound sterling as the basic monetary unit of the UK
sterling.translation: n. 英国货币, 标准纯银\na. 英国货币的, 标准纯银的, 含标准成分的

examples.en: This company has a sterling reputation worldwide.
His supervisor gave him a sterling recommendation.
I found a sterling silver spoon.

stern.definition: n. the rear part of a ship\nn. United States concert violinist (born in Russia in 1920)\ns. severe and unremitting in making demands
stern.translation: n. 尾部, 船尾, 臀\na. 严厉的, 严格的, 坚定的, 坚决的

examples.en: The teacher gave his pupils a stern telling-off.
examples.zh: 老师把学生狠狠地骂了一顿。

examples.en: The teacher gave her pupils a stern telling-off.
examples.zh: 老师把学生狠狠地骂了一顿。

steward.definition: n. someone who manages property or other affairs for someone else\nn. the ship's officer who is in charge of provisions and dining arrangements\nn. an attendant on an airplane
steward.translation: n. 管理人, 招待员, 管家, 乘务员\n[经] 轮船, 飞机的服务员, (财务)管理员

examples.en: You are the steward of your own destiny.
"There it is," said the steward.
"Here you are," the steward says.

stick.definition:
n. an implement consisting of a length of wood
n. a small thin branch of a tree
n. a lever used by a pilot to control the ailerons and elevators of an airplane
n. a rectangular quarter pound block of butter or margarine
stick.translation: n. 棍, 棒, 刺, 枯枝, 茎, 条状物\nvt. 插进, 刺入, 钉住, 伸出, 粘贴, 停止\nvi. 粘住, 停留, 坚持, 陷住, 伸出

examples.en: Tom wrote his name in the sand with a stick.
examples.zh: 汤姆用棍子在沙上写了他的名字。

examples.en: I think you had better stick to your present job.
examples.zh: 我觉得你应该继续做这份工作。

examples.en: The rat was killed by him with a stick.
examples.zh: 他用一根棍子把老鼠打死了。

sticky.definition: s. moist as with undried perspiration and with clothing sticking to the body\ns. covered with an adhesive material
sticky.translation: a. 粘的, 有粘性的, 顽固的

examples.en: I can't get this sticky ball out of my hand.
This sticky tape is no good – it keeps coming off.
Don't leave any sticky or greasy residue in the car.

stiff.definition:
n. an ordinary man
s. not moving or operating freely
s. powerful
r. extremely
stiff.translation: a. 坚硬的, 严厉的, 呆板的, 生硬的, 刚强的, 强烈的, 粘的, 稠的, 艰难的\nn. 死尸, 醉鬼, 钞票\nvt. 不肯付...小费

examples.en: After standing for 6 hours, Antonio's legs became stiff.
examples.zh: Antonio站了六个小时后，腿变得僵硬。

examples.en: Throughout the five years of painful cancer treatments, he managed to keep a stiff upper lip.
examples.zh: 这五年痛苦的癌症治疗他终于坚持下来了。

stigma.definition: n. the apical end of the style where deposited pollen enters the pistil\nn. an external tracheal aperture in a terrestrial arthropod\nn. a skin lesion that is a diagnostic sign of some disease
stigma.translation: n. 耻辱, 污名, 烙印\n[医] 柱头; 小孔, 眼点; 气孔; 小斑; 特征

examples.en: There's a stigma attached to living on a council estate.
Sami spoke out against the stigma against mental health issues.
The stigma surrounding female sexuality weighs heavily on her.

stimulate.definition:
v. act as a stimulant
v. stir the feelings, emotions, or peace of
v. cause to be alert and energetic
v. stir feelings in
stimulate.translation: vt. 刺激, 激励, 鼓舞\nvi. 起刺激作用

examples.en: Tax cuts are often used as a major fiscal tool to stimulate the economy.
examples.zh: 减税常被用作刺激经济的主要财政手段。

examples.en: Coffee and tea stimulate me.
examples.zh: 咖啡和茶使我感到兴奋。

stimulus.definition: n any stimulating information or event; acts to arouse action
stimulus.translation: n. 刺激, 激励, 刺激品\n[医] 刺激特, 刺激

examples.en: Light is the stimulus that causes a flower to open.
Does the Algerian government need a large fiscal stimulus plan?
A nerve cell responds to a slight stimulus.

sting.definition:
n. a kind of pain; something as sudden and painful as being stung
n. a painful wound caused by the thrust of an insect's stinger into skin
v. deliver a sting to
v. cause an emotional pain, as if by stinging
sting.translation: n. 叮, 刺痛, 刺激, 讽刺\nvt. 叮, 刺痛, 刺激, 使苦恼\nvi. 叮, 刺痛

examples.en: I got a bee sting.
examples.zh: 我被蜜蜂蛰了一下。

examples.en: I've just been stung by a bee.
examples.zh: 我刚给蜜蜂蛰了。

examples.en: I was stung by a bee.
examples.zh: 我被蜜蜂蛰了一下。

stipulate.definition: v. specify as a condition or requirement in a contract or agreement; make an express demand or provision in an agreement\nv. give a guarantee or promise of\nv. make an oral contract or agreement in the verbal form of question and answer that is necessary to give it legal force

examples.en: Why wouldn't you stipulate that in the contract?
Did you stipulate that it was to be delivered by August first?
If you stipulate that these things are true, I will sign the contract.

stir.definition:
n. a prominent or sensational but short-lived news event
n. emotional agitation and excitement
v. move an implement through
v. move very slightly
stir.translation: n. 骚动, 轰动, 搅动, 监狱\nvt. 移动, 摇动, 激起, 惹起, 搅拌\nvi. 走动, 传播, 搅拌

examples.en: I don't want to stir up old memories.
examples.zh: 我不愿意勾起久远的回忆。

examples.en: A light breeze stirred the surface of the lake.
examples.zh: 微风吹荡着湖面。

examples.en: She stirred her coffee with a teaspoon.
examples.zh: 她用茶匙搅她的咖啡。

stitch.definition: n. a link or loop or knot made by an implement in knitting, crocheting, embroidery, or sewing\nn. a sharp spasm of pain in the side resulting from running
stitch.translation: n. 一针, 疼痛, 针法, 碎布条, 针脚\nv. 缝, 缝合, 装订

examples.en: A stitch in time saves nine.
examples.zh: 小洞及时补，免遭大洞苦。

stock.definition:
n. the capital raised by a corporation through the issue of shares entitling holders to an ownership interest (equity)
n. the merchandise that a shop has on hand
n. the handle of a handgun or the butt end of a rifle or shotgun or part of the support of a machine gun or artillery gun
n. the reputation and popularity a person has
stock.translation:
n. 树干, 祖先, 血统, 原料, 备料, 库存, 牲畜, 股票, 股份, 保留剧目
a. 存货的, 常备的, 平凡的, 普通的, 股票的, 保留剧目的, 繁殖用的
vt. 装把手于, 进货, 备有, 放牧
vi. 出新芽, 备货, 囤积

examples.en: He's making a lot of money in the stock market.
examples.zh: 他炒股赚很多钱。

examples.en: The company is listed on the Paris stock exchange.
examples.zh: 这家公司在巴黎证券交易所上市了。

examples.en: This company is listed on the Paris stock exchange.
examples.zh: 这家公司在巴黎证券交易所上市了。

stone.definition:
n. building material consisting of a piece of rock hewn in a definite shape for a special purpose
n. an avoirdupois unit used to measure the weight of a human body; equal to 14 pounds
n. the hard inner (usually woody) layer of the pericarp of some fruits (as peaches or plums or cherries or olives) that contains the seed
n. United States jurist who was named chief justice of the United States Supreme Court in 1941 by Franklin D. Roosevelt (1872-1946)
stone.translation: n. 石头, 宝石, 果核, 纪念碑, 结石\nvt. 投扔石子, 铺石头\na. 石的, 石制的, 完全的

examples.en: From a distance, this stone looks like a human face.
examples.zh: 从远看得话，这个石头看起来像人的脸。

examples.en: That way I kill two birds with one stone.
examples.zh: 这样子我一箭双雕。

examples.en: "A rolling stone gathers no moss" is a saying.
examples.zh: “滚石不生苔”是一句谚语。

stop.definition:
n. the event of something ending
n. the act of stopping something
n. a brief stay in the course of a journey
n. a spot where something halts or pauses
stop.translation: n. 停止, 车站, 逗留, 填塞, 障碍, (风琴的)音栓\nvi. 停止, 被塞住\nvt. 塞住, 堵塞, 阻止, 击落, 停止, 终止, 断绝

examples.en: I want you to know I tried to stop Tom.
examples.zh: 我希望你知道我已经试了阻止汤姆。

examples.en: Could you show me the way to the bus stop?
examples.zh: 请问公车站该怎么去？

examples.en: I know that Tom can stop me from doing that.
examples.zh: 我知道汤姆不能阻止我做那件事。

storage.definition: n. the act of storing something\nn. the commercial enterprise of storing goods and materials\nn. (computer science) the process of storing information in a computer memory or on a magnetic tape or disk
storage.translation: n. 存储器, 储藏, 保管, 库存, 仓库\n[计] 存放处; 存储

examples.en: My phone needs to have enough storage for my apps.
examples.zh: 我的手机需要足够存储空间来下载 App。

store.definition: n. a supply of something available for future use\nv. keep or lay aside for future use\nv. find a place for and put away for storage
store.translation:
n. 商店, 贮藏, 仓库, 备用品, 存储器
vt. 储存, 贮藏, 供给
vi. 贮藏
a. 贮藏的, 现成的
[计] 存储器操作; 存储

examples.en: I'll go to the store and buy you some wine.
examples.zh: 我要去商店给你买些酒。

examples.en: There are no hats in that store that fit me.
examples.zh: 那个店里没有合我尺寸的帽子。

examples.en: There were no hats in that store that fit me.
examples.zh: 那个店里没有适合我的帽子。

storm.definition:
n. a violent weather condition with winds 64-72 knots (11 on the Beaufort scale) and precipitation and thunder and lightning
n. a violent commotion or disturbance
n. a direct and violent assault on a stronghold
v. take by force
storm.translation: n. 暴风雨, 骚动, 风波, 风暴, 猛攻\nvi. 起风, 猛冲, 怒吼\nvt. 猛攻

examples.en: We took refuge from the storm in a nearby barn.
examples.zh: 为躲避风暴，我们躲到了附近的一个谷仓内。

examples.en: The weatherman says there is a storm on the way.
examples.zh: 气象学家说会有暴风雨。

examples.en: The town was destroyed by the flood after the storm.
examples.zh: 小镇被暴风雨后的洪水摧毁了。

story.definition: n. a piece of fiction that narrates a chain of related events
story.translation: n. 故事, 小说, 传奇, 描述, 阅历, 经历, 层

examples.en: Is it true or did Tom make that story up?
examples.zh: 这是事实还是Tom编的故事？

examples.en: I am telling a good story to my younger friend.
examples.zh: 跟我的年轻朋友讲一个好听的故事。

examples.en: The saddest part of the story remains to be told.
examples.zh: 这则故事最悲情的部分尚未揭晓。

stove.definition: n. a kitchen appliance used for cooking food\nn. any heating apparatus
stove.translation: n. 火炉, 窑\nvt. 用火炉烤\nstave的过去式和过去分词

examples.en: Don't leave dirty pots and pans on the stove; wash them.
examples.zh: 不要把脏锅碗瓢盆放在炉子上，去洗。

examples.en: A plastic dish will melt on the stove.
examples.zh: 塑料盘子在烤箱里会化的。

examples.en: Clean the stove and oven after cooking.
examples.zh: 烹饪结束后请清洁炉灶和烤箱。

straightforward.definition: s. free from ambiguity\ns. pointed directly ahead
straightforward.translation: a. 笔直的, 率直的, 明确的, 简单的, 直接的

examples.en: People who can express their thoughts in a clear-cut way are very straightforward.
examples.zh: 能够直截了当地表达自己想法的人很直爽。

strain.definition:
n. (physics) deformation of a physical body under the action of applied forces
n. (psychology) nervousness resulting from mental stress
n. injury to a muscle (often caused by overuse); results in swelling and pain
n. an intense or violent exertion
strain.translation: n. 紧张, 拉紧, 张力, 过劳, 扭伤, 血缘, 种, 族, 气质, 曲调, 旋律, 口吻\nvt. 使劳累, 拉紧, 过分使用, 扭伤, 滥用, 曲解, 滤\nvi. 尽力, 努力, 紧拉, 弯曲, 被滤出

examples.en: Tom has been under a great deal of strain lately.
examples.zh: 汤姆最近压力特别大。

examples.en: The rope broke under the strain.
examples.zh: 绳子被拉断了。

examples.en: Though passion may have strained, it must not break our bonds of affection.
examples.zh: 虽然激情可能会褪去，却不容它破坏我们感情上的联系。

strand.definition:
n. a pattern forming a unity within a larger structural whole
n. line consisting of a complex of fibers or filaments that are twisted together to form a thread or a rope or a cable
n. a poetic term for a shore (as the area periodically covered and uncovered by the tides)
n. a street in west central London famous for its theaters and hotels
strand.translation: n. (绳索的)股, 绳, 串, 海滨, 河岸\nvi. 搁浅\nvt. 使搁浅, 使落后, 使陷于困境, 弄断, 搓

examples.en: Because of the blizzard, Tom and Mary were stranded in Boston.
examples.zh: 因为暴风雪，汤姆和玛丽被困在波士顿了。

examples.en: If you were stranded on a desert island, what books would you want to have with you to read?
examples.zh: 如果你被困在一个荒岛上, 你会想要随身带著哪些书来看?

strange.definition: a. being definitely out of the ordinary and unexpected; slightly odd or even a bit weird\ns. not known before
strange.translation: a. 奇怪的, 陌生的, 生疏的, 不熟悉的, 不可思议的, 外行的, 外地的, 异乡的

examples.en: It is strange for Ken not to agree with us.
examples.zh: 肯不同意我们，是件奇怪的事。

examples.en: It may sound strange, but what she said is true.
examples.zh: 听起来或许有点怪，但她说的是真的。

examples.en: Even though it sounds strange, what she said is true.
examples.zh: 虽然听起来很奇怪，但是她说的的确是真的。

stranger.definition: n. anyone who does not belong in the environment in which they are found\nn. an individual that one is not acquainted with
stranger.translation: n. 陌生人, 门外汉\n[法] 局外人, 非当事人, 第三者

examples.en: A stranger is just a friend you haven't met yet.
examples.zh: 所谓陌生人，只是还未相见的友人而已。

examples.en: He treats me as if I am a stranger.
examples.zh: 他把我当成陌生人来看待。

examples.en: He treats me as if I were a stranger.
examples.zh: 他把我当成陌生人来看待。

strap.definition:
n. an elongated leather strip (or a strip of similar material) for binding things together or holding something in position
n. hanger consisting of a loop of leather suspended from the ceiling of a bus or train; passengers hold onto it
n. a band that goes over the shoulder and supports a garment or bag
n. whip consisting of a strip of leather used in flogging
strap.translation: n. 带, 皮带\nvt. (用皮带)捆扎

examples.en: She has this pretty lace nightgown with straps.
examples.zh: 她的这件吊带蕾丝睡衣很漂亮。

examples.en: I'm strapped for cash.
examples.zh: 我缺钱。

strategic.definition: a. relating to or concerned with strategy\ns. highly important to or an integral part of a strategy or plan of action especially in war
strategic.translation: a. 战略的, 战略上的\n[经] 战略的

examples.en: This project offers strategic advantages for Algeria.
examples.zh: 这项专案给阿尔及利亚带来策略性优势。

strategy.definition: n. the branch of military science dealing with military command and the planning and conduct of a war
strategy.translation: n. 战略, 策略\n[经] 战略, 策略

examples.en: China is incorporating Algeria into its Belt and Road strategy.
examples.zh: 中国正将阿尔及利亚纳入「一带一路」战略。

examples.en: Real-time strategy games usually include arcade elements.
examples.zh: 即时策略游戏通常会融入街机元素。

examples.en: Amateurs talk strategy, professionals talk logistics.
examples.zh: 外行谈策略，内行谈后勤。

straw.definition:
n. plant fiber used e.g. for making baskets and hats or as fodder
n. a thin paper or plastic tube used to suck liquids into the mouth
v. cover or provide with or as if with straw
s. of a pale yellow color like straw; straw-colored
straw.translation: n. 稻草, 麦管, 吸管, 一文不值的东西, 草帽\na. 稻草的, 稻草色的, 琐碎的, 无价值的

examples.en: A man of straw is worth a woman of gold.
I am very much attached to this old straw hat.
Will you ask the waitress to bring me a straw?

strawberry.definition: n. sweet fleshy red fruit\nn. any of various low perennial herbs with many runners and bearing white flowers followed by edible fruits having many small achenes scattered on the surface of an enlarged red pulpy berry\nn. a soft red birthmark

examples.en: The strawberry tree is a commonly used landscape plant in this area.
examples.zh: 草莓树是该地区常见的景观植物。

examples.en: Strawberry juice is good for the memory.
examples.zh: 草莓汁对记忆力有利。

examples.en: This ice cream is not strawberry flavoured.
examples.zh: 这个冰淇淋不是草莓味的。

streak.definition:
n. an unbroken series of events
n. a distinctive characteristic
n. a sudden flash (as of lightning)
v. move quickly in a straight line
streak.translation: n. 条理, 斑纹, 倾向\nvt. 加条纹\nvi. 变成条纹, 飞跑

examples.en: Her hair is streaked with gray.
examples.zh: 她的头发中夹有白发。

stream.definition:
n. a natural body of running water flowing on or under the earth
n. dominant course (suggestive of running water) of successive events or ideas
n. something that resembles a flowing stream in moving continuously
v. to extend, wave or float outward, as if in the wind
stream.translation:
n. 水流, 小河, 流出, 趋势, 人潮
vt. 流出, 流动, 展开
vi. 流, 涌, 飘扬
[计] 流

examples.en: It must be dangerous to swim in this rapid stream.
examples.zh: 在这么急的急流里游泳，一定会很危险的。

examples.en: A stream of people came out of the theater.
examples.zh: 剧场里涌出一大群人。

examples.en: He sat next to the stream.
examples.zh: 他坐在溪流旁边。

strength.definition: n. the property of being physically or mentally strong\nn. the condition of financial success
strength.translation: n. 力量, 实力, 强度, 浓度, 人数, 抵抗力\n[化] 强度

examples.en: It is not just to prefer strength to good wisdom.
examples.zh: 相比于智慧更偏爱力量是不公平的。

examples.en: Tom got the job on the strength of your recommendation.
examples.zh: 多亏了你的推荐，汤姆得到了那份工作。

examples.en: War is peace. Freedom is slavery. Ignorance is strength.
examples.zh: 战争即和平，自由即奴役，无知即力量。

strengthen.definition: v. make strong or stronger\nv. gain strength
strengthen.translation: vt. 加强, 变坚固\nvi. 变强, 股票上涨

examples.en: The government should strengthen their army once and for all!
examples.zh: 政府应该彻底加强军队建设！

examples.en: Cultural exchange programs can strengthen friendly relations between neighboring countries.
examples.zh: 文化交流计划可以加强邻国之间的友好关系。

examples.en: It will also help to strengthen the city's economy.
examples.zh: 它也会促进城市的经济发展。

stress.definition:
n. the relative prominence of a syllable or musical note (especially with regard to stress or pitch)
n. special emphasis attached to something
n. difficulty that causes worry or emotional tension
n. (physics) force that produces strain on a physical body
stress.translation: n. 压力, 紧迫, 强调, 重音, 重点, 应力\nvt. 加压力于, 着重, 重读

examples.en: There has been a lot of stress at work lately.
examples.zh: 最近工作压力太大了。

examples.en: Where do you place the stress in the word "Australia"?
examples.zh: “Australia”这个词的重音要放在哪？

examples.en: She is unable to cope with stress.
examples.zh: 她无法应付压力。

stretch.definition:
n. a large and unbroken expanse or distance
n. a straightaway section of a racetrack
n. exercise designed to extend the limbs and muscles to their full extent
n. extension to or beyond the ordinary limit
stretch.translation:
n. 伸展, 张开, 连绵, 一段路, 一段时间
a. 可伸缩的, 弹性的
vt. 伸展, 张开, 曲解, 使过度伸展
vi. 伸展, 延伸
[计] 伸展

examples.en: On the border, there is a stretch of agricultural land.
examples.zh: 边境上有一片农业区。

examples.en: You have to stretch your muscles after swimming in the pool.
examples.zh: 在泳池游完泳后要拉伸肌肉。

examples.en: He stretched out his arm to take the book.
examples.zh: 他伸长了手臂为了能拿到书。

strict.definition:
s rigidly accurate; allowing no deviation from a standard
s (of rules) stringently enforced
a characterized by strictness, severity, or restraint
s incapable of compromise or flexibility
s severe and unremitting in making demands
strict.translation: a. 严厉的, 绝对的, 详尽的, 严格的, 精确的\n[法] 严格的, 精确的, 绝对的

examples.en: There is no need to be so strict.
examples.zh: 用不着这么严格。

examples.en: Mary is on a strict diet, isn't she?
examples.zh: 玛丽在严格节食中，对吗？

examples.en: Tom used to be a strict vegetarian.
examples.zh: 汤姆已然成为了一名严格的素食主义者。

stride.definition: n. significant progress (especially in the phrase "make strides")\nv. walk with long steps\nv. cover or traverse by taking long steps
stride.translation: n. 大步, 步幅, 步态, 进步\nv. 迈大步走, 跨过, 跨

examples.en: Under the teacher's guidance, I took big strides with my studies.
examples.zh: 在老师的指导下，我的学习有了很大的进步。

strike.definition:
n. a group's refusal to work in protest against low pay or bad work conditions
n. an attack that is intended to seize or inflict damage on or destroy an objective
n. a score in tenpins: knocking down all ten with the first ball
n. (baseball) a pitch that the batter swings at and misses, or that the batter hits into foul territory, or that the batter does not swing at but the umpire judges to be in the area over home plate and between the batter's knees and shoulders
strike.translation: n. 罢工, 打击, 殴打\nvt. 打, 撞击, 冲击, 侵袭, 取消, 结算, 打掉, 罢工, 刺透, 使生根, 遇见\nvi. 打, 打击, 抓, 罢工, 搏动, 触礁, 敲, 响, 穿透, 打动

examples.en: No one knows when a severe earthquake will strike Tokyo.
examples.zh: 没有人知道东京甚么时候会发生大地震。

examples.en: We're on strike because the company hasn't improved our wages.
examples.zh: 我们罢工是因为公司没有改善我们的工资。

examples.en: "Will they go on strike again?" "I'm afraid so."
examples.zh: 「他们又要罢工了吗？」「恐怕是的。」

striking.definition:
n the physical coming together of two or more things
n the act of contacting one thing with another
v deliver a sharp blow, as with the hand, fist, or weapon
v have an emotional or cognitive impact upon
v hit against; come into sudden contact with
v make a strategic, offensive, assault against an enemy, opponent, or a target
v indicate (a certain time) by striking
v affect or afflict suddenly, usually adversely
v stop work in order to press demands
v touch or seem as if touching visually or audibly
v attain
v produce by manipulating keys or strings of musical instruments, also metaphorically
v cause to form (an electric arc) between electrodes of an arc lamp
v find unexpectedly
v produce by ignition or a blow
v remove by erasing or crossing out or as if by drawing a line
v cause to experience suddenly
v drive something violently into a location
v occupy or take on
v form by stamping, punching, or printing
v smooth with a strickle
v pierce with force
v arrive at after reckoning, deliberating, and weighing
s sensational in appearance or thrilling in effect
s having a quality that thrusts itself into attention
striking.translation: a. 醒目的, 惊人的, 打击的, 罢工的\n[法] 罢工的, 罢市的, 罢课的

examples.en: The resemblance between Sean and Conner is striking!
examples.zh: Sean 和 Conner 长得真像！

examples.en: The difference is striking.
examples.zh: 差异惊人。

examples.en: Anna's striking almond-shaped eyes, inherited from her Asian lineage, exude a captivating depth and a hint of mystery.
examples.zh: 安娜引人注目的杏仁状眼睛继承了她的亚洲血统，散发著迷人的深度和一丝神秘感。

string.definition:
n. a lightweight cord
n. a tightly stretched cord of wire or gut, which makes sound when plucked, struck, or bowed
n. a sequentially ordered set of things or events or ideas in which each successive member is related to the preceding
n. a linear sequence of symbols (characters or words or phrases)
string.translation:
n. 线, 细绳, 一串, 字符串
vt. 串起, 成串, 收紧, 缚, 扎
vi. 成一串
[计] 字符串, 串

examples.en: Specialists are people who have only one string on their violin.
examples.zh: 专家就好像一台只有一根弦的小提琴一样。

examples.en: I broke a string on my guitar.
examples.zh: 我弄断了我吉他的一根弦。

examples.en: She tied up the parcel with string.
examples.zh: 她用绳子把包裹紧紧绑好了。

strip.definition:
n. a relatively long narrow piece of something
n. artifact consisting of a narrow flat piece of material
n. thin piece of wood or metal
n. a form of erotic entertainment in which a dancer gradually undresses to music
strip.translation: n. 长条, 条状, 带, 脱衣舞\nvt. 脱衣, 被剥去, 剥夺, 拆卸\nvi. 脱衣服

examples.en: I want to slice these potatoes into strips.
examples.zh: 我想把这些土豆切成丝。

examples.en: They played strip poker.
examples.zh: 他们玩脱衣扑克.

examples.en: Tom was stripped to the waist.
examples.zh: 汤姆光着膀子。

stripe.definition:
n. a piece of braid, usually on the sleeve, indicating military rank or length of service
n. a kind or category
n. a narrow marking of a different color or texture from the background
v. mark with stripes
stripe.translation: n. 斑纹, 条纹\n[医] 纹, 条纹

examples.en: I would like to try the blue striped skirt.
examples.zh: 我想试一下那条蓝色条纹裙。

examples.en: Zebra shadows don't have stripes.
examples.zh: 斑马的影子没有条纹。

examples.en: The stripes were horizontal.
examples.zh: 条纹是水平的。

strive.definition: v. to exert much effort or energy
strive.translation: vi. 努力, 奋斗, 斗争

examples.en: No matter how hard I strive, I fail to achieve my parents' requirements.
examples.zh: 不管我怎么努力，也达不到父母的要求。

examples.en: Confidence and courage are not just masculine traits; they are values anyone can strive for.
examples.zh: 自信与勇气不仅是男性特质，也可以是所有人都能追求的价值。

stroke.definition:
n. (sports) the act of swinging or striking at a ball with a club or racket or bat or cue or hand
n. a sudden loss of consciousness resulting when the rupture or occlusion of a blood vessel leads to oxygen lack in the brain
n. a light touch
n. a light touch with the hands
stroke.translation: n. 笔划, 打, 中风, 抚, 摩, 冲程\nvt. 划尾桨, 抚, 摩, 划去\n[计] 笔划

examples.en: Could you tell me the stroke order of the character "老" in the word "年老"?
examples.zh: 你能告诉我“年老”的“老”字的笔顺吗？

examples.en: Tom had a heat stroke.
examples.zh: 汤姆中暑了。

examples.en: An elderly person in my family suddenly fell to the ground; he likely suffered a stroke.
examples.zh: 我家里有个老年人突然倒在地上，大概是中风了。

stroll.definition: v. walk leisurely and with no apparent aim
stroll.translation: n. 闲逛, 漫步\nv. 闲逛, 漫步

examples.en: Spaniards love to stroll around in the evening cool.
examples.zh: 西班牙人最爱在晚上外出散散步、乘乘凉。

examples.en: Friend, how about we stroll through the Chinatown?
examples.zh: 朋友，我请你去唐人街逛逛怎么样？

examples.en: Would you like to take a stroll around the park with me?
examples.zh: 你想陪我逛公园吗？

structural.definition:
a. relating to or caused by structure, especially political or economic structure
a. relating to or having or characterized by structure
s. affecting or involved in structure or construction; not ornamental elements"
s. concerned with systematic structure in a particular field of study
structural.translation: a. 结构的, 建筑的\n[医] 结构的

examples.en: No one should be left behind in Algeria's structural change.
The structural integrity of the building is compromised.
The self does not preexist its structural determination.

structure.definition:
n. a thing constructed; a complex entity constructed of many parts
n. the manner of construction of something and the arrangement of its parts
n. the complex composition of knowledge as elements and their combinations
n. a particular complex anatomical part of a living thing
structure.translation: n. 结构, 构造, 建筑物\nvt. 构成, 组织

examples.en: This is the most massive structure I have ever seen.
examples.zh: 这是我所见过的最大型的构造了。

examples.en: This is the most massive structure I've ever seen.
examples.zh: 这是我所见过的最大型的构造了。

examples.en: The school's tallest structure is that water tower.
examples.zh: 学校最高的建筑就是那个水塔。

struggle.definition: n. an energetic attempt to achieve something\nn. strenuous effort\nv. to exert strenuous effort against opposition
struggle.translation: n. 斗争, 努力, 奋斗\nvi. 努力, 奋斗, 挣扎

examples.en: Tom couldn't tell the difference between play and struggle.
examples.zh: 汤姆分不清游戏与斗争。

examples.en: They are struggling with the goal of wiping out smallpox.
examples.zh: 他们奋斗的目标是消灭天花。

examples.en: In a struggle of power, if you aren't with us, you're against us.
examples.zh: 在权利斗争中，非友即敌。

stubborn.definition: a. tenaciously unwilling or marked by tenacious unwillingness to yield
stubborn.translation: a. 顽固的, 不听话的, 执拗的, 棘手的

examples.en: I have never come across such a stubborn person.
examples.zh: 我从来没碰到过这么倔的人。

examples.en: Facts are stubborn things, but statistics are pliable.
examples.zh: 事实是倔强的，但统计是柔顺的。

examples.en: Why are you being so stubborn?
examples.zh: 你为什么这么倔？

stuff.definition:
n. miscellaneous unspecified objects
n. informal terms for personal possessions
n. senseless talk
n. unspecified qualities required to do or be something
stuff.translation: n. 原料, 要素, 东西, 材料, 素质, 织品, 废物, 废话\nvt. 装填\nvi. 狼吞虎咽

examples.en: There's a lot of stuff in our lo mein.
examples.zh: 我们的拌面里有好多东西。

examples.en: I'm going to get rid of all this stuff.
examples.zh: 我要摆脱这一切。

examples.en: Can't you move your stuff to the other room?
examples.zh: 你不能把你的东西搬去另一个房间吗？

stumble.definition:
v. walk unsteadily
v. miss a step and fall or nearly fall
v. encounter by chance
v. make an error
stumble.translation: n. 绊倒, 蹒跚而行, 失足\nvt. 使绊倒, 使困惑\nvi. 绊倒, 失足, 失策, 犯错, 蹒跚, 踌躇

examples.en: The newborn giraffe stumbled around on rickety legs.
examples.zh: 新生的长颈鹿摇晃著腿跌跌撞撞地走。

examples.en: Tom stumbled back home.
examples.zh: 汤姆跌跌撞撞地回到了家。

stump.definition:
n. the base part of a tree that remains standing after the tree has been felled
n. the part of a limb or tooth that remains after the rest is removed
n. (cricket) any of three upright wooden posts that form the wicket
v. cause to be perplexed or confounded
stump.translation: n. 残株, 树桩, 烟蒂, 讲演台\nvt. 砍断, 挑战, 难住\nvi. 蹒跚而走

examples.en: I'll sit on a tree stump and eat a pie.
There's a tree stump at the bottom of the lake.
The candidate delivered his usual stump speech at the rally.

stun.definition: v. make senseless or dizzy by or as if by a blow\nv. overcome as with astonishment or disbelief
stun.translation: vt. 使昏迷, 使震惊, 打昏\nn. 昏迷, 猛击

examples.en: Everyone in the room was stunned by what happened.
examples.zh: 屋里人都被发生的事惊住了。

examples.en: Everybody in the room was stunned by what happened.
examples.zh: 屋里人都被发生的事惊住了。

examples.en: Grandmother died, leaving the whole family stunned.
examples.zh: 奶奶死了，全家大惊。

stupid.definition: n. a person who is not very bright\na. lacking or marked by lack of intellectual acuity
stupid.translation: a. 愚蠢的, 麻木的

examples.en: Between you and me, I think our boss is stupid.
examples.zh: 我觉得我们老板很蠢，这我就只跟你说。

examples.en: My parents keep arguing about stupid things. It's so annoying!
examples.zh: 我父母整天都在为鸡毛蒜皮的事情吵架，真是烦死人了！

examples.en: I'm not as stupid as you think I am.
examples.zh: 我不像你想的那么傻。

sturdy.translation: a. 强健的, 健全的\n[医] 羊晕倒病, 羊蹒跚病

examples.en: This kind of cloth is both cheap and sturdy.
examples.zh: 这种布既便宜又结实。

examples.en: This is a sturdy handrail.
examples.zh: 那是个坚固的栏杆。

style.definition:
n. a particular kind (as to appearance)
n. (botany) the narrow elongated part of the pistil between the ovary and the stigma
n. editorial directions to be followed in spelling and punctuation and capitalization and typographical display
n. a slender bristlelike or tubular process
style.translation:
n. 风格, 时尚, 文体, 风度, 字体, 类型
vt. 称呼, (根据新款式)设计, 使合潮流
n. 风格, 样式
[计] 风格, 样式

examples.en: Fashions of thirty years ago have come back in style.
examples.zh: 三十年前的时装款式又流行起来了。

examples.en: Viking helmets with horns aren't in style in Scandinavia anymore.
examples.zh: 斯堪的纳维亚现在已经不流行戴维京人那种有角的头盔了。

examples.en: The hair style of the Beatles created a sensation.
examples.zh: 披头士的发型引起了轰动。

subdue.definition:
v put down by force or intimidation
v to put down by force or authority
v hold within limits and control
v get on top of; deal with successfully
v make subordinate, dependent, or subservient
v correct by punishment or discipline
subdue.translation: vt. 使服从, 压制, 减弱, 抑制, 克制

examples.en: The police used tear gas to subdue the protestors.
The policemen caught up with Dan and managed to subdue him.
I could not subdue the desire to laugh.

subject.definition:
n. the subject matter of a conversation or discussion
n. something (a person or object or scene) selected by an artist or photographer for graphic representation
n. (grammar) one of the two main constituents of a sentence; the grammatical constituent about which something is predicated
n. a person who is subjected to experimental or other observational procedures; someone who is an object of investigation
subject.translation:
n. 科目, 主题, 臣民, 主语, 题目, (事物的)经受者, 学科, 受治疗者, 原因, 理由
a. 服从的, 易患...的, 隶属的, 受支配的
adv. 在...条件下
vt. 使隶属, 使受到
[计] 主题, 主体

examples.en: Even our brains are subject to the laws of physics.
examples.zh: 就连我们的头脑也遵守物理法则。

examples.en: Your initial order is subject to a special discount of 5%.
examples.zh: 首次订购可获九五折的特别优惠。

examples.en: We study English, since it is an important subject nowadays.
examples.zh: 我们学习英语，就今天来说是一项重要科目。

subjective.definition: a. taking place within the mind and modified by individual bias
subjective.translation: a. 主观的, 个人的\n[医] 主观的, 自觉的

examples.en: His writing is very subjective.
examples.zh: 他写文章写得很主观。

submarine.definition:
n. a submersible warship usually armed with torpedoes
v. move forward or under in a sliding motion
v. throw with an underhand motion
v. bring down with a blow to the legs
submarine.translation:
n. 潜水艇, 海底生物
a. 海中的, 生长在海中的
vt. 用潜水艇攻击
vi. 在下疾行, 在下滑动

examples.en: Russia is sending battleships, marines, and landing craft tanks against Syria, and submarine equiment against Iran.
examples.zh: 俄罗斯正向叙利亚派遣战舰、海军陆战队和登陆艇坦克，并向伊朗派遣潜舰装备。

submission.definition:
n. something (manuscripts or architectural plans and models or estimates or works of art of all genres etc.) submitted for the judgment of others (as in a competition)
n. the act of submitting; usually surrendering power to another
n. the condition of having submitted to control by someone or something else
n. a legal document summarizing an agreement between parties in a dispute to abide by the decision of an arbiter
submission.translation: n. 屈服, 服从, 谦恭, 呈递, 提交, 意见\n[经] 提交, 提出, 提交公断

examples.en: We have the alternative of death and submission.
examples.zh: 我们要选择是死亡还是臣服。

submit.definition:
v. refer for judgment or consideration
v. put before
v. yield to the control of another
v. yield to another's wish or opinion
submit.translation: vt. 使服从, 使受到, 委托, 提交, 认为\nvi. 屈服, 服从

examples.en: Edit your work better before you submit it, it's sloppy.
examples.zh: 提交工作内容之前请仔细检查，这里有疏忽的地方。

examples.en: The due date for submitting the application is this Friday.
examples.zh: 提交申请的最后期限是星期五。

examples.en: Accepting the other's norms is submitting to the other's power.
examples.zh: 接受对方的准则就是给予他权力。

subordinate.definition:
n. an assistant subject to the authority or control of another
v. rank or order as less important or consider of less value
v. make subordinate, dependent, or subservient
a. lower in rank or importance
subordinate.translation: n. 属下, 附属物\na. 下级的, 次要的, 附属的\nvt. 使居下位, 使服从

examples.en: I was stabbed in the back by my subordinate.
All the other issues are subordinate to this one.
Today isn't subordinate to any country in the world.

subscribe.definition: v. offer to buy, as of stocks and shares\nv. adopt as a belief\nv. receive or obtain regularly
subscribe.translation: vt. 捐献, 签署\nvi. 赞成, 同意, 捐款, 预订, 认购\n[计] 订阅

examples.en: Starting next month, I'm not subscribing to a newspaper.
examples.zh: 下个月开始我不订报纸了。

examples.en: Do you subscribe to any magazines?
examples.zh: 你有订阅任何杂志吗？

examples.en: What newspaper do you subscribe to?
examples.zh: 你订阅了什么报纸?

subscription.definition:
n. a payment for consecutive issues of a newspaper or magazine for a given period of time
n. agreement expressed by (or as if expressed by) signing your name
n. a pledged contribution
n. the act of signing your name; writing your signature (as on a document)
subscription.translation: n. 捐献, 订金, 订阅, 签署, 同意\n[化] 订购

examples.en: All subscriptions must be paid before the end of this year.
examples.zh: 所有订购必须在今年年底前支付款项。

examples.en: The subscription service is available for a fixed monthly fee with a one-month free trial.
examples.zh: 此订阅服务的月费为固定金额，并提供免费试用一个月。

examples.en: The monthly fee for this subscription service is fixed, and it offers a one-month free trial.
examples.zh: 此订阅服务的月费为固定金额，并提供免费试用一个月。

subsequent.definition: a. following in time or order
subsequent.translation: a. 后来的, 接下去的\n[经] 后来的

examples.en: The subsequent effects of the attack decimated the tourism industry there.
I want quick action subsequent to the decision.
Knowledge has been passed down to subsequent generation.

subsequently.definition: r. happening at a time subsequent to a reference time

examples.en: The agreement was subsequently renegotiated, but details were not disclosed.
Subsequently, the US Air Force assumed control in 1948.
Several witnesses subsequently recanted their statements claiming coercion.

subsidy.definition: n. a grant paid by a government to an enterprise that benefits the public
subsidy.translation: n. 补助金, 津贴\n[经] 补助金, 津贴, 补贴

examples.en: She turned down the subsidy that I offered.
examples.zh: 她拒绝了我的资助。

substance.definition: n. the real physical matter of which a person or thing consists\nn. material of a particular kind or constitution\nn. a particular kind or species of matter with uniform properties
substance.translation: n. 物质, 实质, 主旨, 资产, 本质, 牢固\n[化] 物质

examples.en: The substance is light enough to float on the water.
examples.zh: 这种物质很轻，可以浮在水面上。

examples.en: Water and ice are the same substance in different forms.
examples.zh: 水和冰虽然形态不同，但其实是同一种物质。

examples.en: It’s a communication medium, not a substance or specific activity.
examples.zh: 网络是一个相通的渠道，而不是物质或具体的活动。

substantial.definition: s. having a firm basis in reality and being therefore important, meaningful, or considerable\na. having substance or capable of being treated as fact; not imaginary
substantial.translation: n. 重要材料(或事物), 有实际价值的东西\na. 实质上的, 物质的, 有内容的, 结实的

examples.en: Layla robbed a substantial amount of money from the bank.
Algeria is gifted with a substantial amount of natural resources.
Using cash makes you think money is truly substantial.

substitute.definition:
n. a person or thing that takes or can take the place of another
n. an athlete who plays only when a starter on the team is replaced
v. put in the place of another; switch seemingly equivalent items
v. be a substitute
substitute.translation:
n. 代理, 代理人, 代用品, 代替者, 代替物
vt. 代替
vi. 替代, 取代, 代用
a. 代替的, 代用的, 代用品的
[计] 置换; 替代

examples.en: Then I'll work on the principle that deference is no substitute for obedience.
examples.zh: 那我就恭敬不如从命啦。

examples.en: He substituted for his father.
examples.zh: 子承父业。

examples.en: She substituted margarine for butter.
examples.zh: 她用人造黄油代替了黄油。

subtle.definition: s. able to make fine distinctions
subtle.translation: a. 敏锐的, 精细的, 狡猾的, 稀薄的, 灵巧的, 微妙的\n[医] 锐敏的; 精细的

examples.en: There are subtle differences between the two pictures.
examples.zh: 这两张图片之间有细致的差异。

suburb.definition: n. a residential district located on the outskirts of a city
suburb.translation: n. 市郊住宅区, 郊区, 边缘

examples.en: The other day something horrible happened in a Tokyo suburb.
examples.zh: 前几天，东京郊外发生了件可怕的事情。

examples.en: Helen and Kathy rented an apartment in a suburb of Tokyo.
examples.zh: 海伦和凯蒂在东京郊区租了个套间。

examples.en: A car is a must for life in the suburbs.
examples.zh: 要住在郊区的话，汽车是必需的。

suburban.definition: a. relating to or characteristic of or situated in suburbs
suburban.translation: a. 郊外的, 郊区的, (贬)偏狭的, 土气的, 见识不广的\nn. 郊区居民

examples.en: Yanni lived in a normal suburban house in Algiers.
The house is located in a quiet suburban neighborhood.
This distillery looks like a suburban mall bookstore from the nineties.

succeed.definition: v. attain success or reach a desired goal\nv. be the successor (of)
succeed.translation: vi. 成功, 继承, 继续\nvt. 继承, 接替

examples.en: You have to make efforts if you are to succeed.
examples.zh: 如果你想成功，必先付出努力。

examples.en: He had lost all faith in his ability to succeed.
examples.zh: 他完全丧失了能成功的信心。

examples.en: If you are to succeed, you must start studying now.
examples.zh: 如果你要成功, 你必须现在开始学习。

success.definition: n. an event that accomplishes its intended purpose\nn. an attainment that is successful\nn. a state of prosperity or fame
success.translation: n. 成功, 成就, 胜利

examples.en: Overall, the movie was a success from script to screen.
examples.zh: 总的来说，这部电影从剧本到银幕是成功的。

examples.en: Your help is indispensable for the success of the scheme.
examples.zh: 没有你帮忙，计划就不能成功了。

examples.en: Education is the path to happiness, peace, righteousness, and success.
examples.zh: 教育是通往幸福、和平、正义与成功的道路。

succession.definition:
n. a group of people or things arranged or following in order
n. the action of following in order
n. (ecology) the gradual and orderly process of change in an ecosystem brought about by the progressive replacement of one community by another until a stable climax is established
n. acquisition of property by descent or by will
succession.translation: n. 连续, 继承权, 继位, 演替, 地层次序\n[法] 继承, 继承权, 继位

examples.en: After a succession of warm days, the weather became cold.
Man approaches the unattainable truth through a succession of errors.
They have won for the third year in succession.

successive.definition: s in regular succession without gaps
successive.translation: a. 继承的, 连续的\n[经] 接续承运人; 连续的

examples.en: It rained five successive days.
examples.zh: 雨一连下了五天。

successor.definition: n. a person who follows next in order\nn. a thing or person that immediately replaces something or someone\nn. a person who inherits some title or office
successor.translation: n. 继承者, 接任者\n[计] 后继

examples.en: Two is the only prime whose successor is prime.
The matter of his successor is still under debate.
I want to leave things in good order for my successor.

suck.definition:
v. draw into the mouth by creating a practical vacuum in the mouth
v. draw something in by or as if by a vacuum
v. attract by using an inexorable force, inducement, etc.
v. be inadequate or objectionable
suck.translation: vt. 吸, 吮, 吸入, 吮吸, 吸收\nvi. 吸, 吸奶\nn. 吸, 吸入, 吮吸

examples.en: You suck dude! I have to tell you everything!
examples.zh: 你好烂哦！ 我什么事都需要跟你讲！

examples.en: It must suck to be you.
examples.zh: 你真可怜。

examples.en: I sucked up the dust on the floor with a vacuum cleaner.
examples.zh: 我用吸尘机把地上的灰尘吸掉了。

sudden.definition: a. happening without warning or in a short space of time
sudden.translation: n. 突然, 忽然\na. 突然的, 意外的, 快速的

examples.en: I was surprised at the news of his sudden death.
examples.zh: 他突然过世的消息让我感到惊讶。

examples.en: There was a sudden drop in the temperature last night.
examples.zh: 昨天晚上气温突然下降

examples.en: Avoid sudden movements around the rabbit, they can startle them.
examples.zh: 避免在兔子旁边突然做出动作，以免吓到牠们。

sue.definition: n. French writer whose novels described the sordid side of city life (1804-1857)
sue.translation: vt. 控告, 起诉, 请求\nvi. 提出诉讼, 提出请求

examples.en: At last, John and Sue decided to cut the apple into halves.
examples.zh: 约翰和苏最后决定把苹果切成两半。

examples.en: Sue checked in at the Royal Hotel.
examples.zh: 苏在皇家饭店登记投宿。

examples.en: Sue and John decided to get married.
examples.zh: Sue 和 John 决定结婚。

suffer.definition:
v. undergo or be subjected to
v. undergo (as of injuries and illnesses)
v. experience (emotional) pain
v. get worse
suffer.translation: vt. 遭受, 经历, 忍受\nvi. 受痛苦, 受损害

examples.en: All humanity will suffer if a nuclear war breaks out.
examples.zh: 一旦爆发核战争，受苦的将会是全人类。

examples.en: He is suffering from a bad cold in the nose.
examples.zh: 他患了重感冒。

examples.en: Do you suffer from diseases that require medication?
examples.zh: 你是否身患需服药的疾病？

sufficient.definition: a. of a quantity that can fulfill a need or requirement but without being abundant
sufficient.translation: a. 充分的, 足够的\n[法] 充分的, 足够的

examples.en: I haven't yet collected sufficient materials to write a book.
examples.zh: 我还没有收集到足够的材料来写一本书。

examples.en: I have not yet collected sufficient materials to write a book.
examples.zh: 我还没有收集到足够的材料来写一本书。

examples.en: We have sufficient evidence to prove this hypothesis.
examples.zh: 我们有充分的理由论证这个假设。

sugar.definition: n. a white crystalline carbohydrate used as a sweetener and preservative\nv. sweeten with sugar
sugar.translation: n. 糖, 糖块, 甜言蜜语\nvt. 加糖于, 使甜蜜, 粉饰, 美化\nvi. 制成糖

examples.en: To make a cake, you need egg, butter and sugar.
examples.zh: 要做蛋糕，你要用到鸡蛋，黄油和糖。

examples.en: We need flour, sugar and eggs to make this cake.
examples.zh: 我们需要面粉、砂糖和鸡蛋来做这个蛋糕。

examples.en: The store sells foodstuffs, such as butter, cheese, and sugar.
examples.zh: 这家店卖的是牛油、奶酪、砂糖之类的食品。

suggest.definition: v. imply as a possibility\nv. call to mind
suggest.translation: vt. 提议, 建议, 促成, 暗示, 启发, 使人想起\n[法] 建议, 提出, 提议

examples.en: I suggest that he come to Poland a bit earlier.
examples.zh: 我建议他早一点儿到波兰来。

examples.en: If you're bored, I suggest you go to the cinema.
examples.zh: 如果你感到无聊，我建议你去电影院。

examples.en: Could you possibly suggest a way to solve the problem?
examples.zh: 你能提出解决问题的方法吗？

suggestion.definition:
n. an idea that is suggested
n. a proposal offered for acceptance or rejection
n. persuasion formulated as a suggestion
n. the sequential mental process in which one thought leads to another by association
suggestion.translation: n. 提议, 意见\n[医] 暗示

examples.en: He thought she spoke reasonably, so he accepted her suggestion.
examples.zh: 他觉得她说得很有道理，于是接受了她的建议。

examples.en: Mike said a few words by way of suggestion.
examples.zh: 麦克以建议的口气说了些话。

examples.en: He's proposing a suggestion for altering the research method.
examples.zh: 他提出改革研究方法的意见。

suicide.definition: n. the act of killing yourself\nn. a person who kills himself intentionally
suicide.translation: n. 自杀, 自杀者\nv. 自杀\na. 自杀的

examples.en: How frustrated must a person be to commit suicide?
examples.zh: 一个人得遇到多大的挫折才会自杀？

examples.en: According to the newspaper, he committed suicide.
examples.zh: 据报纸上说，他自杀了。

examples.en: I heard that Tom attempted suicide.
examples.zh: 我听说汤姆自杀没成。

suit.definition:
n. a set of garments (usually including a jacket and trousers or skirt) for outerwear all of the same fabric and color
n. (slang) a businessman dressed in a business suit
n. a petition or appeal made to a person of superior status or rank
n. playing card in any of four sets of 13 cards in a pack; each set has its own symbol and color
suit.translation: n. 套装, 诉讼, 请求, 起诉, 套, 组\nvt. 适合, 使适应\nvi. 合适, 相称

examples.en: I can't find the waistcoat of my three piece suit.
examples.zh: 我找不到我三件套的背心。

examples.en: Your shoes do not go with the suit.
examples.zh: 你的鞋子和衣服不合衬。

examples.en: Tom only wears a suit on special occasions.
examples.zh: 汤姆只在特殊场合穿西装。

suitable.definition: s. meant or adapted for an occasion or use
suitable.translation: a. 适当的, 相配的\n[法] 合适的, 适宜的, 适当的

examples.en: Her acute observation skills make her a very suitable photographer.
examples.zh: 她因为敏锐的观察力，很适合当一名摄影师。

examples.en: Choose a suitable satellite image as the base map.
examples.zh: 选择合适的卫星图做为底图。

examples.en: I like using these goods; they are very suitable for me.
examples.zh: 我喜欢用这些产品，非常适合我。

suite.definition: n. a musical composition of several movements only loosely connected\nn. apartment consisting of a series of connected rooms used as a living unit (as in a hotel)\nn. a matching set of furniture
suite.translation: n. 随员, 套房, (一)组, (一)套, 组曲, 继之而来的事\n[电] 程序组

examples.en: This suite is three times larger than my condominium.
Pietro went through the entire suite and found nothing.
Tom rented a suite in one of Boston's most expensive hotels.

sum.definition:
n. a quantity of money
n. a quantity obtained by the addition of a group of numbers
n. the final aggregate
n. the whole amount
sum.translation:
n. 总数, 总和, 金额, 概要, 顶点
vt. 总计, 概括
vi. 合计
[计] 系统实用程序和维护

examples.en: The sum of two plus three plus four is nine.
examples.zh: 二加三加四的和是九。

examples.en: She had only a small sum of money.
examples.zh: 她当时只有一丁点儿钱。

examples.en: The old man contributed a large sum of money to the poor.
examples.zh: 那位老者捐了一大笔钱去帮助穷人。

examples.en: Summarize the contents in 60 English words.
examples.zh: 请把内容浓缩至六十个英文字以内。

summary.definition: n. a brief statement that presents the main points in a concise form
summary.translation: n. 摘要, 概要\na. 摘要的, 简略的\n[计] 摘要; 概要

examples.en: The following is a summary of the President's speech.
examples.zh: 下面是总统讲话的概要。

summit.definition: n. a meeting of heads of governments\nv. reach the summit (of a mountain)
summit.translation: n. 顶点, 最高阶层, 最高级会议\na. 政府首脑的, 最高级的

examples.en: The summit of Mt. Fuji was covered in snow.
examples.zh: 富士山顶盖满了雪。

examples.en: Who first reached the summit of Mt. Everest?
examples.zh: 最先登上珠穆朗玛峰的人是谁？

examples.en: The air is thin at the summit.
examples.zh: 山顶上空气稀薄。

summon.definition: v. call in an official matter, such as to attend court\nv. ask to come
summon.translation: vt. 召唤, 召集, 号召, 振奋, 唤起, 鼓起\n[经] 传唤, 传讯

examples.en: He gained the power to summon ghost trains.
examples.zh: 他获得了召唤幽灵列车的能力。

sun.definition:
n. the star that is the source of light and heat for the planets in the solar system
n. a person considered as a source of warmth or energy or glory etc
n. any star around which a planetary system revolves
v. expose one's body to the sun
sun.translation: n. 太阳, 日, 日光, 阳光\nvt. 晒\nvi. 晒太阳

examples.en: The Sun is in the center of the solar system.
examples.zh: 太阳在太阳系的中心。

examples.en: Without the light of the sun, we could see nothing.
examples.zh: 如果没有了阳光，我们就甚么也看不见了。

examples.en: It takes 165 years for Neptune to orbit around the sun.
examples.zh: 海王星绕行太阳一周要花一百六十五年。

sunlight.definition: n. the rays of the sun
sunlight.translation: n. 日光\n[医] 日光, 太阳光

examples.en: Skin shouldn't be exposed to sunlight for too long.
examples.zh: 不要把皮肤长时间暴露在阳光里。

examples.en: The icy road sparkled in the sunlight.
examples.zh: 结冰的道路在阳光下闪闪发亮。

examples.en: The hills are bathed in sunlight.
examples.zh: 丘陵沐浴在阳光下。

superb.translation: a. 极度的, 华丽的, 极好的

examples.en: It goes without saying that he is a superb pianist.
The weather is superb, and the sea is calm.
I didn't have breakfast today, but dinner was superb.

superficial.definition: a. concerned with or comprehending only what is apparent or obvious; not deep or penetrating emotionally or intellectually\na. of, affecting, or being on or near the surface\ns. of little substance or significance
superficial.translation: n. 表面, 外表\na. 表面的, 肤浅的, 面积的

examples.en: You have to acquire real skills, not just superficial knowledge.
examples.zh: 你要学的是实实在在的技能，而不单是表面的知识。

examples.en: He has only a superficial knowledge of Japanese.
examples.zh: 他对日文只是略懂皮毛。

examples.en: One must have conviction in law, or its existence will be superficial only.
examples.zh: 法律必须被信仰，否则形同虚设。

superintendent.definition: n. a caretaker for an apartment house; represents the owner as janitor and rent collector
superintendent.translation: n. 监督人, 主管人, 主日学校校长\n[经] 监督人, 主管人(部门)

examples.en: The building's superintendent has set up a meeting with the residents.
The public housing superintendent used to receive bribes from the aging tenant.
Ah, Superintendent Chalmers! Welcome. I hope you're prepared for an unforgettable luncheon!

superior.definition:
n. one of greater rank or station or quality
n. the head of a religious community
n. a town in northwest Wisconsin on Lake Superior across from Duluth
a. of high or superior quality or performance
superior.translation: n. 长者, 占优势的人, 上级\na. 上级的, 出众的, 高傲的

examples.en: Father has now got a superior position in his office.
examples.zh: 现在父亲在他的办公室已经得到了一个上级的地位。

examples.en: This carpet is superior to that one in quality.
examples.zh: 这地毯在质量上比那个好得多。

examples.en: He is superior to his opponents in all respects.
examples.zh: 他在各方面都超出他的对手。

supermarket.definition: n. a large self-service grocery store selling groceries and dairy products and household goods
supermarket.translation: n. 超级市场\n[经] 超级市场, 自助售货商店

examples.en: Could you tell how to get to the nearest supermarket?
examples.zh: 你能告诉我怎么去最近的超市吗？

examples.en: Currently, my sister works as a cashier at a supermarket.
examples.zh: 目前，我妹妹在一家超市当收银员。

examples.en: Please go to the supermarket to buy some fruit.
examples.zh: 请你去超市买些水果来。

supervise.definition: v watch and direct\nv keep tabs on; keep an eye on; keep under surveillance
supervise.translation: v. 监督, 管理, 指导

examples.en: Tom was hired to supervise the production of Mary's music video.
While she is writing, her dad will supervise.
"Would you be willing to supervise this test?"

supervision.definition: n. management by overseeing the performance or operation of a person or group
supervision.translation: n. 监督, 管理\n[经] 监督, 管理

examples.en: His heart was weak and he needed constant medical supervision.
Don't touch the stove or oven without adult supervision.
Under supervision, he looks after his clients much better.

supper.definition: n. a light evening meal; served in early evening if dinner is at midday or served late in the evening at bedtime\nn. a social gathering where a light evening meal is served

examples.en: I have my supper at a quarter past seven.
examples.zh: 我在七时十五分吃晚饭。

examples.en: I don't eat supper because I want to lose some weight.
examples.zh: 我不吃晚饭因为我想减肥。

examples.en: I watched the news on TV after supper.
examples.zh: 我吃过晚饭后打开电视看了一会儿新闻。

supplement.definition: n. a quantity added (e.g. to make up for a deficiency)\nv. add as a supplement to what seems insufficient\nv. serve as a supplement to
supplement.translation: n. 补充物, 增刊, 补充, 补遗, 补编, 附录, 补角\nvt. 补充, 增补

examples.en: From now on, you should exercise regularly. I bought some health supplements for you to try.
examples.zh: 这以后要经常锻炼，我买了点补药给你吃吃看。

supply.definition: n. an amount of something available for use\nn. offering goods and services for sale\nv. give something useful or necessary to
supply.translation: n. 补给, 供给, 供应品\nvt. 补给, 供给, 提供, 补充\nvi. 替代

examples.en: However vast the darkness, we must supply our own light.
examples.zh: 不论黑暗如何辽阔，我们都必须提供自身的光明。

examples.en: The store can supply us with anything we need.
examples.zh: 这家商店可以提供所有我们需要的东西。

examples.en: They monopolized the supply market and drastically raised prices.
examples.zh: 他们垄断了原物料供应，并开天价。

support.definition:
n. the activity of providing for or maintaining by supplying with money or necessities
n. aiding the cause or policy or interests of
n. something providing immaterial assistance to a person or cause or interest
n. a military operation (often involving new supplies of men and materiel) to strengthen a military force or aid in the performance of its mission
support.translation: n. 支持, 支撑, 援助, 供养, 支撑物\nvt. 支援, 支撑, 帮助, 支持, 忍受, 供养, 证实\n[计] 后援; 支持

examples.en: I want to ensure my phone has good customer support.
examples.zh: 我想要确定手机能有优秀的客户服务。

examples.en: With this little money, I can't even support my family.
examples.zh: 靠这点钱，我连自己的家庭都养不活。

examples.en: I worked hard in order to support my family.
examples.zh: 我努力工作养家糊口。

supporter.definition: n. a person who backs a politician or a team etc.
supporter.translation: n. 支持者, 后盾, 迫随者, 护身织物\n[法] 支持者, 赡养者, 抚养者

examples.en: Rev. King and his supporters were threatened.
examples.zh: 金牧师和他的支持者们受到威胁。

examples.en: We are looking for supporters.
examples.zh: 我们寻找支持者。

suppose.translation: vt. 推想, 假设, 以为, 想像, 假定\nvi. 料想

examples.en: I could tell Tom the truth, I suppose.
examples.zh: 我看我能告诉汤姆真实情况。

examples.en: Tom never told me what I was supposed to do.
examples.zh: 汤姆从来没有告诉我应该怎么做。

examples.en: Where do you suppose you'll spend your vacation?
examples.zh: 你认为你会到哪儿度假？

supposedly.definition: r believed or reputed to be the case
supposedly.translation: adv. 想象上, 看上去像, 被认为是, 恐怕, 按照推测

examples.en: Supposedly, his father once betrayed China.
examples.zh: 据说他的父亲曾经是汉奸。

suppress.definition: v. to put down by force or authority\nv. put out of one's consciousness\nv. reduce the incidence or severity of or stop
suppress.translation: vt. 镇压, 使止住, 禁止, 抑制, 查禁\n[法] 镇压, 平定, 禁止出版

examples.en: Heathers help to suppress weeds in your garden.
examples.zh: 石楠花有助于抑制花园里的杂草。

examples.en: Is France trying to suppress Algeria's development?
examples.zh: 法国是在试图压制阿尔及利亚的发展吗？

examples.en: Tom tried to suppress a smile.
examples.zh: 汤姆试著克制笑容。

supreme.definition: s. final or last in your life or progress\ns. highest in excellence or achievement\ns. greatest or maximal in degree; extreme
supreme.translation: n. 至高, 霸权\na. 至高的, 终极的, 极端的, 最大的

examples.en: The embassy is located next to the Supreme Court.
examples.zh: 大使馆就在最高法院旁边。

examples.en: Cyber activists want to meet with the Supreme Leader.
examples.zh: 网络积极分子想跟最高领袖见面。

sure.definition:
s. physically secure or dependable
s. (of persons) worthy of trust or confidence
s. infallible or unfailing
s. certain not to fail
sure.translation: a. 确信, 必然的, 必定的\nadv. 当然, 确实地, 无疑地

examples.en: He is poor, to be sure, but he is happy.
examples.zh: 他确实很穷，但是他很幸福。

examples.en: I'm not sure as to when he will turn up.
examples.zh: 我不知道他甚么时候会出现。

examples.en: Are you sure you don't want to sleep on it?
examples.zh: 你确定你不想睡在它上面吗？

surface.definition:
n. the outer boundary of an artifact or a material layer constituting or resembling such a boundary
n. the extended two-dimensional outer boundary of a three-dimensional object
n. the outermost level of the land or sea
n. a superficial aspect as opposed to the real nature of something
surface.translation:
n. 面, 表面, 水面, 外表, 平面
a. 表面的, 外观的, 肤浅的, 水面上的
vt. 使成平面, 使浮出水面
vi. 浮出水面, 呈现, 在地面上工作

examples.en: Your lips are soft like the surface of a cactus.
examples.zh: 你的嘴唇软绵绵的，就像仙人掌的表皮一样。

examples.en: A fallen leaf floated on the surface of the water.
examples.zh: 水面浮着一片落叶。

examples.en: One fifth of the earth's surface is covered by permafrost.
examples.zh: 地球表面的五分之一被冻土覆盖了。

surge.definition: n. a sudden or abrupt strong increase\nv. see one's performance improve
surge.translation:
n. 巨涌, 汹涌, 澎湃
vi. 汹涌, 澎湃, 颠簸, 猛冲, 突然放松
vt. 使汹涌奔腾, 急放
[计] 电压尖峰

examples.en: Demand for occupational therapy has surged in recent years.
examples.zh: 这几年对作业疗法的需求在迅速增长。

examples.en: Due to the rainstorm, the river water surged over the river banks.
examples.zh: 因为暴雨，河水暴涨漫过河岸。

surgeon.definition: n. a physician who specializes in surgery
surgeon.translation: n. 外科医生, 军医, 船医\n[医] 外科医师

examples.en: My father is an expert surgeon.
examples.zh: 我父亲是一名外科专家。

examples.en: There are two doctors in his circle of friends, a surgeon and an ophthalmologist.
examples.zh: 他的圈子里有两人是医生，一个是外科医生，另一个是眼科医生。

examples.en: He's an excellent brain surgeon.
examples.zh: 他是一个优秀的脑外科医生。

surgery.definition: n. the branch of medical science that treats disease or injury by operative procedures\nn. a room where a doctor or dentist can be consulted
surgery.translation: n. 外科, 手术, 手术室, 换球术

examples.en: I developed a tumor in my stomach, which required surgery.
examples.zh: 我得了胃肿瘤，必须动手术切除。

examples.en: Cosmetic surgery is not covered by most insurance plans.
examples.zh: 大部份的保险计划不包含整容手术。

examples.en: This clinic is doing laser surgery.
examples.zh: 这个诊所正在做激光手术。

surplus.definition: n a quantity much larger than is needed\ns more than is needed, desired, or required
surplus.translation: n. 剩余, 过剩, 盈余\na. 过剩的, 剩余的

examples.en: Our surplus has swelled by nearly ten percent in this quarter.
examples.zh: 我们公司今季的赤字上涨了差不多一成。

surprise.definition:
n. the astonishment you feel when something totally unexpected happens to you
n. a sudden unexpected event
n. the act of surprising someone
v. cause to be surprised
surprise.translation: n. 惊奇, 奇袭, 诧异\nvt. 使惊奇, 撞见, 奇袭

examples.en: To my surprise, he easily came up with a plan.
examples.zh: 令我吃惊的是，他很容易就想出了一个方案。

examples.en: Her surprise was so great that she could not speak.
examples.zh: 她惊讶得说不出话来。

examples.en: "What are you doing here?" he asked me in surprise.
examples.zh: “你怎么来了？”他惊讶地问我。

surrender.definition: n. the delivery of a principal into lawful custody\nv. give up or agree to forgo to the power or possession of another\nv. relinquish possession or control over
surrender.translation: vt. 交出, 放弃, 使投降, 让与\nvi. 投降, 自首\nn. 交出, 放弃, 投降

examples.en: Are we going to surrender to these monsters?
examples.zh: 我们要向这个怪兽投降吗？

examples.en: Sami had no choice but to surrender.
examples.zh: 萨米只有投降一途

examples.en: I would rather die than surrender.
examples.zh: 我宁死不降。

surround.definition: v. extend on all sides of simultaneously; encircle
surround.translation: vt. 包围, 环绕, 围绕\nn. 围绕物

examples.en: Japan is a country surrounded by the sea on all sides.
examples.zh: 日本是个四面环海的国家。

examples.en: He was surrounded by a throng of reporters.
examples.zh: 他被一大群记者包围著。

examples.en: The garden was surrounded by a wooden fence.
examples.zh: 花园被木栅栏围了起来。

surrounding.definition:
v extend on all sides of simultaneously; encircle
v envelop completely
v surround so as to force to give up
v surround with a wall in order to fortify
s closely encircling

examples.en: I've been to the area surrounding Shanghai.
examples.zh: 我去过上海周围的地方。

examples.en: The surrounding area was very quiet.
examples.zh: 周围的地区非常安静。

surveillance.definition: n. close observation of a person or group (usually by the police)
surveillance.translation: n. 监视, 监督\n[电] 侦测

examples.en: He paid the prostitute the fee without being aware of the surveillance camera.
examples.zh: 他在不知有监控录像的情况下支付了妓女服务费用。

examples.en: Tom didn't notice the surveillance camera.
examples.zh: 汤姆没有注意到监控摄像头。

survey.definition:
n. a detailed critical inspection
v. consider in a comprehensive way
v. look over carefully or inspect
v. make a survey of; for statistical purposes
survey.translation: n. 纵览, 视察, 测量, 俯瞰, 调查\nvt. 审视, 视察, 俯瞰, 通盘考虑\nvi. 测量土地

examples.en: A recent survey shows that the number of smokers is decreasing.
examples.zh: 最近的一项调查显示吸烟的人数减少了。

examples.en: According to the latest survey, 99% of employees want a free iPad.
examples.zh: 根据最新的调查，99%的员工想要一个免费的iPad。

examples.en: The results of the Chinese Academy of Sciences' survey are like this.
examples.zh: 中国科学院的调查结果是这样的。

survival.definition: n. a state of surviving; remaining alive\nn. a natural process resulting in the evolution of organisms best adapted to the environment\nn. something that survives
survival.translation: n. 生存, 残存, 幸存者\na. 赖以生存的

examples.en: This medicine will increase the survival rate of the patients.
examples.zh: 这个药品会提高病人的存活率。

examples.en: Air pollution will be a threat to our survival.
examples.zh: 空气污染将会威胁我们的生存。

examples.en: Food, clothing and shelter are the foundations of survival.
examples.zh: 衣食住是生存的基础。

survive.definition: v. continue to live through hardship or adversity\nv. continue in existence after (an adversity, etc.)
survive.translation: vt. 比...活得长, 生存, 生还, 幸免于\nvi. 活下来, 幸存

examples.en: Small businesses will have to tighten their belts to survive.
examples.zh: 中小企业要勒紧裤带才能存活。

examples.en: Why do they say you have to learn English to survive?
examples.zh: 怎么会有人认为不懂英语就不能生存？

examples.en: I can't survive without air conditioning in the summer.
examples.zh: 我夏天没有空调会死。

susceptible.definition: a. (often followed by `of' or `to') yielding readily to or capable of\ns. easily impressed emotionally
susceptible.translation: a. 易受影响的, 易感动的, 容许...的\n[法] 易感的, 易受影响的, 容许

examples.en: She was susceptible to colds.
examples.zh: 她易患感冒。

suspect.definition: n. someone who is under suspicion\nv. imagine to be the case or true or probable\nv. hold in suspicion; believe to be guilty
suspect.translation: n. 被怀疑者, 嫌疑犯\na. 令人怀疑的, 不可信的, 可疑的\nv. 怀疑, 猜想

examples.en: I suspect they water down the beer in that pub.
examples.zh: 我怀疑那家酒馆的啤酒兑水了。

examples.en: I suspect that Tom will never agree to do that.
examples.zh: 我怀疑汤姆永远不会同意那样做。

examples.en: I suspect that Tom is tired of doing that.
examples.zh: 我怀疑汤姆已经厌烦这么做了。

suspend.definition:
v. hang freely
v. cause to be held in suspension in a fluid
v. bar temporarily; from school, office, etc.
v. make inoperative or stop
suspend.translation: vt. 悬, 吊, 使悬浮, 暂停, 中止, 推迟\nvi. 暂停, 中止, 悬浮, 停止偿付债务\n[计] 暂停

examples.en: The lamp was suspended from the branch of a tree.
examples.zh: 灯笼在树枝上吊着。

examples.en: The earth is just a sphere suspended in space.
examples.zh: 地球只不过是悬浮在太空中的一个球体。

examples.en: I've heard that if you default on the water rates your water supply will be suspended, is that true?
examples.zh: 听说不交水费就会被停水，是真的吗？

suspense.definition: n. apprehension about what is going to happen\nn. an uncertain cognitive state\nn. excited anticipation of an approaching climax
suspense.translation: n. 悬疑, 焦虑, 悬念, 悬而不决\n[经] 未定, 暂记

examples.en: Come on, tell us. Don't keep us in suspense.
The two part episode's cliffhanger had me in suspense.
That's supposed to keep you in suspense until you see the movie.

suspension.definition:
n. a mixture in which fine particles are suspended in a fluid where they are supported by buoyancy
n. an interruption in the intensity or amount of something
n. a mechanical system of springs or shock absorbers connecting the wheels and axles to the chassis of a wheeled vehicle
n. the act of suspending something (hanging it from above so it moves freely)
suspension.translation: n. 悬挂, 暂停, 中止\n[化] 悬浮; 悬浮体; 悬浮液

examples.en: What the hell is this suspension training at the gym?
In Lisbon there is a suspension bridge made of steel.
Daniel was let off with a month of suspension.

suspicious.definition: s openly distrustful and unwilling to confide\ns not as expected
suspicious.translation: a. 可疑的, 多疑的, 怀疑的\n[法] 怀疑的, 令人怀疑的, 可疑的

examples.en: Tom is suspicious of Mary even though he declares otherwise.
examples.zh: 汤姆虽然说了一套，但依然怀疑玛丽。

examples.en: I am suspicious that this is an illegal taxi.
examples.zh: 我怀疑这是辆黑车。

examples.en: Tom didn't seem to be as suspicious as Mary seemed to be.
examples.zh: 汤姆没有玛丽那么可疑。

sustain.definition: v. supply with necessities and support\nv. admit as valid
sustain.translation: vt. 承受, 支持, 供养, 继续, 忍受, 蒙受, 证实, 准许\n[电] 持续

examples.en: Tom sustained serious burns and had to go to the hospital.
examples.zh: 汤姆严重烧伤，不得不去医院治疗。

examples.en: I sustain my family.
examples.zh: 我赚钱养家。

examples.en: We sustained significant losses.
examples.zh: 我们遭受了重大损失。

sustainable.translation: a. 足可支撑的, 养得起的, 可以忍受的

examples.en: New Zealand students have developed sustainable materials made from cabbage tree leaves and flax that could soon be used to make high-performance skis, kayaks and skateboards.
examples.zh: 纽西兰学生开发出由高丽菜树叶和亚麻制成的永续材料，很快就能用于制造高性能滑雪板、皮划艇和滑板。

swallow.definition:
n. a small amount of liquid food
n. the act of swallowing
n. small long-winged songbird noted for swift graceful flight and the regularity of its migrations
v. pass through the esophagus as part of eating or drinking
swallow.translation: n. 燕子, 吞咽, 喉\nvt. 咽, 淹没, 吞没, 耗尽, 轻信, 忍受, 抑制\nvi. 吞下, 咽下

examples.en: I can't swallow these tablets without a drink of water.
examples.zh: 不喝水我咽不下这些药片。

examples.en: If I don't drink a swig of water, I can't swallow these tablets.
examples.zh: 不喝水我咽不下这些药片。

examples.en: Many swallows will come soon from the south.
examples.zh: 许多燕子不久就要从南方飞来了。

swamp.definition: n. low land that is seasonally flooded; has more woody plants than a marsh and better drainage than a bog\nn. a situation fraught with difficulties and imponderables\nv. drench or submerge or be drenched or submerged
swamp.translation: n. 沼泽, 进退两难的困境\nvt. 淹没, 击溃, 清除, 使陷于沼泽\nvi. 陷于沼泽, 淹没

examples.en: He lives alone in a little cottage in the swamp.
examples.zh: 他独自一人住在沼泽地里的一栋小屋里。

examples.en: I don't mean to swamp you.
examples.zh: 我不想把你淹死。

swap.definition: v. move (a piece of a program) into memory, in computer science
swap.translation: n. 以货易货\nv. 交换, 替换, 交易\n[计] 交换

examples.en: I swapped a camera for a guitar.
examples.zh: 我用一台照相机交换一把吉他。

swear.definition: v. promise solemnly; take an oath\nv. make a deposition; declare under oath
swear.translation: vt. 发誓, 咒骂, 使宣誓\nvi. 发誓, 诅咒\nn. 诅咒, 誓言

examples.en: I swear I will never do such a thing.
examples.zh: 我发誓我不会做这种事。

examples.en: I swear that I'll never do such a thing.
examples.zh: 我发誓我不会做这种事。

examples.en: If you swear reckless oaths, lightning will strike you.
examples.zh: 乱发誓会遭雷劈的。

sweat.definition: n. condensation of moisture on a cold surface\nv. excrete perspiration through the pores in the skin
sweat.translation: n. 汗, 汗水, 水珠, 焦急\nvi. 出汗, 渗出, 冒出水气, 结水珠, 烦恼, 懊恼\nvt. 使出汗, 流出, 榨出, 使汗流浃背

examples.en: He wiped the sweat off his face.
examples.zh: 他擦去了脸上的汗水。

examples.en: He wiped the sweat from his face.
examples.zh: 他擦去了脸上的汗水。

examples.en: The sweat was dripping off my brow.
examples.zh: 汗水从我的额头上落下。

sweater.definition: n. a crocheted or knitted garment covering the upper part of the body
sweater.translation: n. 毛衣, 毛线衫, 运动衫, 出汗者\n[化] 发汗器

examples.en: I like the gray sweater more than the purple one.
examples.zh: 比起紫色的毛衣，我更喜欢灰色的毛衣。

examples.en: Take a sweater with you so you don't catch a cold.
examples.zh: 为了不感冒，请带上这件毛衣。

examples.en: The boy wearing the blue sweater is Tom.
examples.zh: 穿著蓝色毛衣的男孩就是汤姆。

sweep.definition:
n. a wide scope
n. a long oar used in an open boat
n. a movement in an arc
v. move with sweeping, effortless, gliding motions
sweep.translation: n. 扫除, 打扫, 肃清, 视野, 范围, 全胜\nvt. 扫除, 掸去, 猛拉, 扫荡, 肃清, 冲走, 刮起, 环视, 掠过, 扫射\nvi. 扫, 打扫, 袭击, 席卷, 扫视, 掠过

examples.en: Spring in the north sends gales to sweep the roads.
