examples.zh: 北方的春天送来狂风扫路。

examples.en: Don't forget to sweep the kitchen clean.
examples.zh: 记住把厨房打扫干净。

examples.en: A blast of cold air swept through the house.
examples.zh: 冷空气疾风席卷整栋房子。

sweet.definition:
n. English phonetician; one of the founders of modern phonetics (1845-1912)
n. a food rich in sugar
n. the taste experience when sugar dissolves in the mouth
a. having or denoting the characteristic taste of sugar
sweet.translation: n. 甜蜜, 糖果, 情人\na. 甜的, 芳香的, 悦耳的, 漂亮的, 和蔼的, 不咸的, 灵活的, 轻快的

examples.en: I've got to stop eating such sweet ice cream.
examples.zh: 我必须停止吃那么甜的冰激凌。

examples.en: Those grapes look sweet, but in fact they're sour.
examples.zh: 那些葡萄看起来很甜，但其实是酸的。

examples.en: I don't like drinking beverages that are too sweet.
examples.zh: 我不喜欢喝太甜的饮料。

swell.definition:
n. the undulating movement of the surface of the open sea
n. a rounded elevation (especially one on an ocean floor)
n. a crescendo followed by a decrescendo
v. increase in size, magnitude, number, or intensity
swell.translation:
n. 增大, 隆起的部分, 巨浪, 肿胀
a. 优秀的, 一流的
vi. 增大, 膨胀, 肿胀, 增强, 骄傲
vt. 使膨胀, 使增大, 使上涨, 使骄傲

examples.en: Our surplus has swelled by nearly ten percent in this quarter.
examples.zh: 我们公司今季的赤字上涨了差不多一成。

examples.en: How long have your cheeks been swollen?
examples.zh: 你的腮帮子肿了多久了？

examples.en: My hands and legs are swollen.
examples.zh: 我的手和脚都肿了。

swift.definition: n. United States meat-packer who began the use of refrigerated railroad cars (1839-1903)\nn. an English satirist born in Ireland (1667-1745)\nn. a small bird that resembles a swallow and is noted for its rapid flight
swift.translation: n. 褐雨燕, 快速爬行的小蜥蜴, 蝙蝠蛾, 大滚筒\na. 迅速的, 快的, 敏捷的, 立刻的\nadv. 迅速地, 敏捷地

examples.en: Life is short and time is swift.
examples.zh: 人生苦短，岁月如梭。

examples.en: The stream is not very swift.
examples.zh: 水流不是很急。

swim.definition:
v. travel through water
v. be dizzy or giddy
v. be covered with or submerged in a liquid
v. move as if gliding through water
swim.translation: n. 游泳, 漂浮, 潮流, 眩晕\nvi. 游泳, 游, 漂浮, 浸, 覆盖, 充溢, 大量拥有, 旋转, 眩晕\nvt. 游过, 使浮起

examples.en: As a boy, I used to swim in the pond.
examples.zh: 我还是个小男孩时常去池塘游泳。

examples.en: Tom is going to ask Mary if she can swim.
examples.zh: 汤姆要问玛莉会不会游泳。

examples.en: I could swim well even when I was a child.
examples.zh: 我很小的时候就游得很好了。

swing.definition:
n. a state of steady vigorous action that is characteristic of an activity
n. mechanical device used as a plaything to support someone swinging back and forth
n. a sweeping blow or stroke
n. changing location by moving back and forth
swing.translation:
n. 摇摆, 振幅, 音律, 节奏, 涨落, 秋千, 旋转, 行动自由
vi. 摇摆, 悬挂, 旋转, 大摇大摆地走, 转向
vt. 挥舞, 使旋转, 使转向, 悬挂, 吊运
a. 旋转的, 悬挂的, 强节奏爵士音乐的

examples.en: Mennad always has those mood swings.
examples.zh: 梅纳德总是情绪波动很大。

examples.en: Chris swung his sword!
examples.zh: 克里斯扬起他的剑。

switch.definition:
n. control consisting of a mechanical or electrical or electronic device for making or breaking or changing the connections in a circuit
n. hairpiece consisting of a tress of false hair; used by women to give shape to a coiffure
n. railroad track having two movable rails and necessary connections; used to turn a train from one track to another or to store rolling stock
n. a flexible implement used as an instrument of punishment
switch.translation:
n. 开关, 电闸, 转换, 软枝, 鞭子, 道岔
vt. 转变, 切换, 摆动, 转换, 使转轨
vi. 转换, 变换, 摆动
[计] 开关; 翻转; 转移

examples.en: I can't turn it on, because the switch is broken.
examples.zh: 因为开关坏了，我没法儿把它打开。

examples.en: Tom's game is in development for PC, PS4 and Switch.
examples.zh: 汤姆的游戏正在为 PC、PS4 和 Switch 开发。

examples.en: Switch off the light. I can't get to sleep.
examples.zh: 把灯关了。我睡不着。

sword.definition: n. a cutting or thrusting weapon that has a long metal blade and a hilt with a hand guard
sword.translation: n. 刀, 剑, 战争, 武力, 剑状物

examples.en: Make the hoe your sword, and the sword your hoe.
examples.zh: 化锄为剑，化剑为锄。

examples.en: Fear is more harmful than the sharpest of swords.
examples.zh: 恐惧比利剑更伤人。

examples.en: "Dad, this a real sword?" "Of course, it is a duel after all."
examples.zh: “爸爸，这是真的剑吗？”“当然，毕竟这是一场对决。”

syllable.definition: n. a unit of spoken language larger than a phoneme
syllable.translation: n. 音节\nvt. 分成音节\n[计] 字节

examples.en: The accent in "guitar" falls on the second syllable.
examples.zh: 「Guitar」一字的重音在第二音节。

examples.en: How many syllables are in this word?
examples.zh: 这个词有多少个音节？

examples.en: How many syllables does this word have?
examples.zh: 这个词有多少个音节？

syllabus.definition: n an integrated course of academic studies
syllabus.translation: n. 摘要, 提纲, 课程表, 教学大纲\n[医] 摘要, 要目

examples.en: I watched the first lecture and read the syllabus.
I don't have a syllabus to teach Berber.
He reviewed the syllabus for the new term.

symbol.definition: n. an arbitrary sign (written or printed) that has acquired a conventional significance\nn. something visible that by association or convention represents something else that is invisible
symbol.translation: n. 符号, 象征, 代号, 信条\n[计] 符号; 码元

examples.en: The belt became a symbol of fear for me.
examples.zh: 这条腰带对我来说成为了恐惧的象征。

examples.en: I don't know what this symbol stands for.
examples.zh: 我不知道这个符号代表什么意思。

examples.en: Mt. Fuji is a symbol of Japan.
examples.zh: 富士山是日本的象征。

symbolic.definition: a. relating to or using or proceeding by means of symbols\na. using symbolism
symbolic.translation: a. 象征的, 符号的\n[电] 符号化

examples.en: Even people who don't believe in the Catholic church venerate the Pope as a symbolic leader.
examples.zh: 甚至是不相信天主教的人也把教皇敬为一个象征性的领导者。

symbolize.definition: v. represent or identify by using a symbol; use symbols
symbolize.translation: vt. 符号化, 用符号表现\nvi. 采用象征, 使用符号

examples.en: In literary works, night-blooming jasmine is often used to symbolize longing and tenderness.
examples.zh: 文学作品中常用夜来香来象征思念与柔情。

examples.en: The hammer and sickle symbolizes communism.
examples.zh: 锤子与镰刀代表共产主义。

symmetry.definition: n. (mathematics) an attribute of a shape or relation; exact reflection of form on opposite sides of a dividing line or plane\nn. balance among the parts of something
symmetry.translation: n. 对称, 匀称\n[化] 对称; 对称性; 对称现象

examples.en: Cephalopods are marine animals characterised by tentacles and bilateral body symmetry.
By architectural symmetry, Emmet means geometric symmetry combined with aesthetic uniformity.
Before we examine Emmet's theory, we must clarify the concept of 'internal symmetry.'

sympathetic.definition:
a. of or relating to the sympathetic nervous system
a. expressing or feeling or resulting from sympathy or compassion or friendly fellow feelings; disposed toward
a. (of characters in literature or drama) evoking empathic or sympathetic feelings
s. having similar disposition and tastes
sympathetic.translation: a. 有同情心的, 合意的, 赞成的\nn. 交感神经, 容易感受的人

examples.en: Mary is more sympathetic to me than Tom is.
I doubt very seriously that Tom will be sympathetic.
Tom told Mary that she should quit pretending to be sympathetic.

sympathize.definition: v. share the feelings of; understand the sentiments of\nv. be understanding of
sympathize.translation: vi. 同情, 怜悯, 同意, 体谅

examples.en: I sympathize with you.
examples.zh: 我同情你。

examples.en: Kate sympathized with him.
examples.zh: Kate很同情他。

sympathy.definition: n. an inclination to support or be loyal to or to agree with an opinion\nn. sharing the feelings of others (especially feelings of sorrow or anguish)\nn. a relation of affinity or harmony between people; whatever affects one correspondingly affects the other
sympathy.translation: n. 同情, 赞同, 怜悯, 慰问, 吊唁\n[医] 交感[作用], 同感[作用], 感应, 同情

examples.en: I feel no sympathy for Tom.
examples.zh: 我不同情汤姆。

examples.en: Everybody showed sympathy toward the prisoner.
examples.zh: 每个人都对囚犯表示同情。

examples.en: I don't need your sympathy.
examples.zh: 我不需要你的同情。

symposium.definition: n. a meeting or conference for the public discussion of some topic especially one in which the participants form an audience and make presentations
symposium.translation: n. 讨论会, 座谈会, 专题报告会, 专题论文集

examples.en: Tom is attending a writers' symposium in Boston.
I'm at a musicians' symposium.
The symposium was a little rougher than usual: "Never again," said Socrates the morning after.

symptom.definition: n. (medicine) any sensation or change in bodily function that is experienced by a patient and is associated with a particular disease\nn. anything that accompanies X and is regarded as an indication of X's existence
symptom.translation: n. 症状, 征候, 征兆\n[医] 症状

examples.en: For how long will I continue to have these symptoms?
examples.zh: 这种症状在我身上将会持续多久？

examples.en: She took Chinese medicine, which relieved her symptoms.
examples.zh: 她吃了中药，减轻了她的症状。

examples.en: If these drugs are stopped abruptly, then some withdrawal symptoms may occur.
examples.zh: 如果这些药突然被停了，那可能会出现一些戒断症状。

syndrome.definition: n. a complex of concurrent things\nn. a pattern of symptoms indicative of some disease
syndrome.translation: n. 并发症状, 综合征, 同时存在的事物\n[计] 校验子; 并发位

examples.en: Depression is common among young adults who have Asperger syndrome.
All of her children were born with Down syndrome.
In Brazil the prevalence of Asperger's Syndrome may reach 0.5%.

synthesis.definition: n. the process of producing a chemical compound (usually by the union of simpler chemical compounds)\nn. the combination of ideas into a complex whole
synthesis.translation: n. 综合, 组织, 综合体\n[化] 合成

examples.en: Phosphorylation is an important step in the synthesis of ATP.
Love, in fact, is the agent of universal synthesis.
The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the organelle responsible for lipid synthesis.

synthetic.definition:
n. a compound made artificially by chemical reactions
a. involving or of the nature of synthesis (combining separate elements to form a coherent whole) as opposed to analysis
a. systematic combining of root and modifying elements into single words
a. of a proposition whose truth value is determined by observation or facts
synthetic.translation: n. 合成物质\na. 综合(性)的, 人造的, 合成的

examples.en: German is a synthetic language.
examples.zh: 德语是综合语。

system.definition:
n. instrumentality that combines interrelated interacting artifacts designed to work as a coherent entity
n. a group of independent but interrelated elements comprising a unified whole
n. (physical chemistry) a sample of matter in which substances in different phases are in equilibrium
n. a complex of methods or rules governing behavior
system.translation: n. 系统, 体系, 制度, 方式, 秩序, 分类原则\n[计] 系统; 体制; 体系

examples.en: The Sun is in the center of the solar system.
examples.zh: 太阳在太阳系的中心。

examples.en: Linux is a free operating system; you should try it.
examples.zh: Linux是一个免费的操作系统。你应该去试用一下。

examples.en: Windows is the most used operating system in the world.
examples.zh: Windows是世界上使用得最多的操作系统。

systematic.definition: a. characterized by order and planning
systematic.translation: a. 有系统的, 分类上的, 体系的\n[医] 系统的, 系的, 分类的

examples.en: Genocide is the systematic effort to exterminate an entire people.
Human rights violations, misogyny and exclusion are widespread and systematic.
We'll begin a systematic search of the town.

salon.definition: n. gallery where works of art can be displayed\nn. a shop where hairdressers and beauticians work\nn. elegant sitting room where guests are received
salon.translation: n. 大会客室, 大厅, 客厅, 交谊室, 沙龙, 美术展览馆, 画廊, 美容院, 发廊

examples.en: Why don't you go to a salon to meet people?
Sami went over to the other side of the salon.
Mary went to the beauty salon to get a manicure.

sanctuary.definition: n. a consecrated place where sacred objects are kept
sanctuary.translation: n. 圣所(指教堂、寺院等), 耶路撒冷的神殿, 避难所\n[法] 庇护所, 避难所, 教堂

examples.en: The USS Monitor was designated the first National Marine Sanctuary on January 30, 1975.
examples.zh: 莫尼特号战舰于 1975 年 1 月 30 日被指定为美国第一个国家海洋保护区。

examples.en: This is a bird sanctuary.
examples.zh: 这是鸟类保护区。

scaffold.definition: n. a platform from which criminals are executed (hanged or beheaded)\nn. a temporary arrangement erected around a building for convenience of workers\nv. provide with a scaffold for support
scaffold.translation: n. 脚手架, 绞刑台\n[化] 脚手架

examples.en: Construction scaffolding will temporarily occlude the view from your balcony.
This is the tallest scaffolding I've ever seen in my life.
Tom fell off the scaffolding while he was painting the house.

scald.definition: n. a burn cause by hot liquid or steam\nn. the act of burning with steam or hot water\nv. treat with boiling water
scald.translation: n. 烫伤, 烫洗\nv. 烫伤, 烫洗

examples.en: Tom scalded himself with boiling water.
examples.zh: 汤姆被开水烫伤了。

scalp.definition: n. the skin that covers the top of the head\nv. sell illegally, as on the black market\nv. remove the scalp of
scalp.translation: v. 剥头皮\nn. 头皮, 战利品

examples.en: My scalp is very itchy.
examples.zh: 我的头皮非常痒。

scam.translation: n. 骗局, 诡计；故事

examples.en: In retrospect, I should've known that it was a scam.
Don't let him bamboozle you into falling for his scam.
I wonder if this is some sort of scam.

scenic.definition: s. used of locations; having beautiful natural scenery\na. of or relating to the stage or stage scenery
scenic.translation: a. 风景好的, 戏剧性的, 舞台的, 布景的\nn. 风光影片, 风景照片

examples.en: This place is famous for its scenic beauty.
examples.zh: 这个地方以风景优美闻名。

examples.en: There are many scenic places in Xinjiang.
examples.zh: 新疆有许多风景优美的地方。

examples.en: Switzerland is famous for its scenic beauty.
examples.zh: 瑞士以它的风景优美而闻名。

scripture.definition: n. any writing that is regarded as sacred by a religious group
scripture.translation: n. 圣经, 圣经的一节, 圣经的一句, 铭文

examples.en: I cannot forbid a person to marry several wives, for it does not contradict Scripture.
examples.zh: 我不能禁止一个人娶好几个妻子，因为这与圣经不矛盾。

shimmer.definition: n. a weak and tremulous light\nv. shine with a weak or fitful light\nv. give off a shimmering reflection, as of silk
shimmer.translation: n. 微光, 闪光\nvi. 闪烁\nvt. 使闪烁

examples.en: On a clear October day, Naini Lake shimmers in the afternoon sun as boatmen row tourists across the hill resort’s prime attraction nestled amid lush, pine-clothed Himalayan peaks.
examples.zh: 在一个晴朗的十月天，奈尼湖在午后阳光下波光粼粼，船夫划桨载著游客穿过这片山区度假胜地最核心的景观，草木繁茂、松林覆盖的喜马拉雅山峰将其包围。

simplicity.definition: n. the quality of being simple or uncompounded\nn. a lack of penetration or subtlety\nn. absence of affectation or pretense
simplicity.translation: n. 单纯, 简朴, 朴素, 坦率, 天真\n[计] 简明性

examples.en: The truth and simplicity of nature is always the most important foundation of noteworthy art.
examples.zh: 大自然的真实和质朴往往是值得注意的艺术中最重要的基石。

smuggle.definition: v. import or export without paying customs duties
smuggle.translation: vt. 偷运, 走私, 私运\nvi. 走私

examples.en: The tunnel was used to smuggle contraband across the border.
Tom smuggled a bottle of whiskey into Mary's hospital room.
She attempted to smuggle diamonds into Algeria.

solvent.definition: n. a liquid substance capable of dissolving other substances\na. capable of meeting financial obligations
solvent.translation: n. 溶剂\na. 有偿付能力的, 有溶解力的

examples.en: An aqueous solution is one where water is the solvent.
Can I use this solvent to dilute my sample?
My responsibility is to keep the company solvent.

soprano.definition:
n. a female singer
n. the highest female voice; the voice of a boy before puberty
n. the pitch range of the highest female voice
s. having or denoting a high range
soprano.translation: n. 女高音, 最高音部, 女高音歌手\na. 女高音的

examples.en: Tom is a bass and Mary is a soprano.
Tom wanted to buy a soprano sax, but couldn't afford one.
Caroline became a well known soprano and began to sing professionally.

spa.definition: n a health resort near a spring or at the seaside\nn a fashionable hotel usually in a resort area\nn a place of business with equipment and facilities for exercising and improving physical fitness
spa.translation: n. 矿泉, 温泉浴场, 矿泉治疗地\n[计] 软件出版者协会

examples.en: The health spa was the hotel’s primary amenity.
The outdoor spa at this hot spring is wonderful.
The spa has a sauna and hot tub.

speciality.definition: n an asset of special worth or utility\nn a distinguishing trait\nn the special line of work you have adopted as your career
speciality.translation: n. 专长, 擅长, 特种技能, 详细说明, 特性, 特产, 专业\n[化] 特制品

examples.en: Mu shu pork is my speciality.
examples.zh: 木须肉是我的拿手菜。

examples.en: So-called regional specialities are things prized by out-of-towners but spurned by locals.
examples.zh: 所谓特产，就是外地人奉之为宝，本地人嗤之以鼻的东西。

spice.definition: n. aromatic substances of vegetable origin used as a preservative\nn. any of a variety of pungent aromatic vegetable substances used for flavoring food\nv. make more interesting or flavorful
spice.translation: n. 香料, 药料, 香气, 调味品, 情趣, 少许\nvt. 加香料, 使添趣味

examples.en: You smell it. Do five spice tea eggs smell good?
examples.zh: 你闻闻香味，五香茶叶蛋香不香？

examples.en: This store has a variety of spices.
examples.zh: 这家商店有各种香料。

examples.en: Capsicum is one of my favorite spices.
examples.zh: 辣椒是我最喜欢的香料之一。

stalk.definition:
n. a slender or elongated structure that supports a plant or fungus or a plant part or plant organ
n. a hunt for game carried on by following it stealthily or waiting in ambush
n. the act of following prey stealthily
n. a stiff or threatening gait
stalk.translation: n. 茎, 追踪, 高视阔步\nvi. 悄悄靠近, 蹑手蹑脚地走近, 蔓延, 高视阔步\nvt. 追踪, 搜索

examples.en: The lion is stalking its prey.
examples.zh: 狮子在跟踪它的猎物。

examples.en: Thoreau coveted the plant's strong purple stalk for a cane, and the robins eat its dark crimson-juiced berries.
examples.zh: 梭罗垂涎于这种植物强壮的紫色茎秆，将其制成藤条，而知更鸟则以深红色汁液的浆果为食。

startling.definition: s. so remarkably different or sudden as to cause momentary shock or alarm

examples.en: Doctors have discovered some startling facts.
examples.zh: 医生发现了一些令人吃惊的事实。

stray.definition: n. an animal that has strayed (especially a domestic animal)\nv. wander from a direct course or at random\ns. (of an animal) having no home or having wandered away from home
stray.translation: n. 走失的家畜, 浪子\na. 迷途的, 偶然的\nvi. 迷路, 彷徨, 流浪

examples.en: Tom has found another stray dog.
examples.zh: 汤姆又遇到野狗。

examples.en: He's careful of stray dogs.
examples.zh: 他对流浪狗很小心。

streamline.translation: n. 流线, 流线型\nvt. 使成流线型, 使合理化

examples.en: From now on I want to attempt to streamline management.
Streamline your localization process with a translation management solution (TMS).
The mayor of New York made an effort to streamline municipal government.

strife.definition: n. bitter conflict; heated often violent dissension
strife.translation: n. 争吵, 竞争, 冲突

examples.en: Strife is the rock on which the party split.
This is nothing other than stirring up ethnic strife.
My strife for learning archaic words has no demarcation.

suffice.definition: v. be sufficient; be adequate, either in quality or quantity
suffice.translation: vi. 足够, 有能力\nvt. 满足

examples.en: Would it suffice if I came around 7?
examples.zh: 我七点左右来就可以了吧？

sulfur.definition: n. an abundant tasteless odorless multivalent nonmetallic element; best known in yellow crystals; occurs in many sulphide and sulphate minerals and even in native form (especially in volcanic regions)
sulfur.translation: n. 硫, 硫磺\nvt. 用硫磺处理

examples.en: Sulfur burns with a blue flame.
examples.zh: 硫磺燃烧著蓝色的火焰。

sunburn.definition: n. redness of the skin caused by exposure to the rays of the sun\nv. get a sunburn by overexposure to the sun
sunburn.translation: n. 日炙, 晒斑, 晒焦, 晒黑\nvt.vi. (使)晒黑, (使)晒得退色, (使)晒焦

examples.en: Christine stayed in the shade all day, because she didn't want to get a sunburn.
examples.zh: Christine整天待在阴凉的地方，因为她不想被晒伤。

examples.en: If you don't want to put on sunscreen, that's your problem. Just don't come complaining to me when you get a sunburn.
examples.zh: 你不想涂防晒霜是你的问题，但是晒伤了不要来抱怨。

superstition.definition: n. an irrational belief arising from ignorance or fear

examples.en: Religion is just organised superstition with a bestseller.
examples.zh: 宗教不过是有组织的迷信加上一本畅销书。

examples.en: Such a ridiculous superstition no longer exists.
examples.zh: 这种荒谬的迷信已不复存在了。

examples.en: Superstitions derive from the inability of men to acknowledge that coincidences are merely coincidences.
examples.zh: 迷信之所以存在，是因为人无法接受巧合只是巧合而已。

supremacy.definition: n power to dominate or defeat
supremacy.translation: n. 至高无上, 霸权地位, 优势, 至上\n[法] 至高权力, 无上权力, 霸权

examples.en: Why does Tom always act personally attacked when white supremacy is mentioned?
Are we not ourselves creating our successors in the supremacy of the earth?
Banning religious symbols in a government that gets days off for several Christian holidays is just Christian supremacy.

suspicion.definition: n. the state of being suspected\nn. being of a suspicious nature
suspicion.translation: n. 怀疑, 觉察, 嫌疑\n[法] 怀疑, 疑心, 嫌疑

examples.en: He was under suspicion of being a spy.
examples.zh: 人们怀疑他是间谍。

examples.en: I have a suspicion about his death.
examples.zh: 我觉得他的死有点可疑。

examples.en: Suspicion is destructive of friendship.
examples.zh: 怀疑会毁掉友情。

server.definition: n. (court games) the player who serves to start a point\nn. (computer science) a computer that provides client stations with access to files and printers as shared resources to a computer network\nn. utensil used in serving food or drink
server.translation: n. 服伺者, 上菜用具, 发球员\nn. 服务器\n[计] 服务器, 服务器启动程序, 服务台程序

examples.en: Heads up! The server will shut down at midnight.
examples.zh: 注意了！服务器半夜要停机。

examples.en: The server reboot is scheduled at 9 o'clock this evening.
examples.zh: 服务器重启预定在今晚9点。

examples.en: I need to configure this server with an appropriate firewall system.
examples.zh: 我该在这个服务器上设置一个防火墙。

syntax.definition: n. the grammatical arrangement of words in sentences\nn. a systematic orderly arrangement\nn. studies of the rules for forming admissible sentences
syntax.translation: n. 句法, 语法, 句子构造\n[计] 句法, 语法

examples.en: The syntax of Python scripts is very simple.
examples.zh: Python脚本的语法很简单。

shareholder.definition: n someone who holds shares of stock in a corporation
shareholder.translation: n. 股东\n[法] 股东, 股票持有人

examples.en: The main shareholder holds twenty percent of the company's equity.
If I were a shareholder, I'd be upset.
Tom is the majority shareholder in the company.

startup.definition: n. the act of setting in operation

examples.en: He wants to know how to start a startup.
Their investment in the startup turned out to be a dud.
Are you comfortable working in a fast-paced startup?

sparrow.definition: n. any of several small dull-colored singing birds feeding on seeds or insects

examples.en: I aimed at a sparrow, but shot down a goose.
examples.zh: 瞄准麻雀, 击中鹅。

examples.en: The sparrow is singing in the trees.
examples.zh: 麻雀正在树上唱歌。

squirrel.definition: n. a kind of arboreal rodent having a long bushy tail\nn. the fur of a squirrel
squirrel.translation: n. 松鼠, 松鼠毛皮\nvt. 贮藏

examples.en: If you were a squirrel, what would you do?
examples.zh: 如果你是只松鼠，你会怎么做？

examples.en: The squirrel advanced against the strong wind.
examples.zh: 松鼠在前面顶著强风。

examples.en: This squirrel has a nut allergy.
examples.zh: 这只松鼠对坚果过敏。

salmon.definition:
n. any of various large food and game fishes of northern waters; usually migrate from salt to fresh water to spawn
n. a tributary of the Snake River in Idaho
n. flesh of any of various marine or freshwater fish of the family Salmonidae
n. a pale pinkish orange color
salmon.translation: n. 鲑鱼, 大麻哈鱼\n[医] 鲑

examples.en: The quality of salmon being sold here is the best.
examples.zh: 这里卖的鲑鱼是品质最好的。

examples.en: Salmon lay their eggs in fresh water.
examples.zh: 三文鱼在淡水中产卵。

examples.en: I want half of a salmon.
examples.zh: 我要半条鲑鱼。

shark.definition:
n. any of numerous elongate mostly marine carnivorous fishes with heterocercal caudal fins and tough skin covered with small toothlike scales
n. a person who is ruthless and greedy and dishonest
n. a person who is unusually skilled in certain ways
v. play the shark; act with trickery
shark.translation: n. 鲨鱼, 骗子\nv. 诈骗

examples.en: Sharks are sensitive to electrical impulses as well as sound.
examples.zh: 鲨鱼对电子信号和噪音很敏感。

examples.en: The skin of a shark is much rougher than that of a tuna fish.
examples.zh: 鲨鱼的皮比鲔鱼的皮粗糙多了。

examples.en: I'm gonna feed you to the sharks.
examples.zh: 我要让你下海喂鲨鱼。

snail.definition: n. freshwater or marine or terrestrial gastropod mollusk usually having an external enclosing spiral shell\nv. gather snails
snail.translation: n. 蜗牛, 行动迟缓的人, 脑筋迟钝的人, 蜗形凸轮\nvt. (蜗牛般)缓慢地打发(时间)\nvi. 缓慢移动

examples.en: The snail drew in its feelers.
examples.zh: 蜗牛把触角缩了回去。

examples.en: The snail draws in its feelers.
examples.zh: 这只蜗牛将触角缩了回去。

examples.en: The snail retreated into its shell.
examples.zh: 蜗牛缩进壳里去了。

sonnet.definition: n. a verse form consisting of 14 lines with a fixed rhyme scheme\nv. praise in a sonnet\nv. compose a sonnet

examples.en: Writing a haiku is easier than writing a sonnet.
A sonnet is framed poetry. It has beauty in form and expression.
A sonnet is a kind of poem.

saucepan.definition: n. a deep pan with a handle; used for stewing or boiling
saucepan.translation: n. (长柄有盖)深平底锅, 炖锅

examples.en: Melt the butter in a saucepan at low heat; reserve.
Melt chocolate and shortening in a saucepan over low heat.
Ziri asked Rima if he could borrow her saucepan.

spatula.definition: n. a turner with a narrow flexible blade\nn. a hand tool with a thin flexible blade used to mix or spread soft substances
spatula.translation: n. 刮刀, 压舌片, 匙突\n[医] 药刀, 软膏刀; 铲; 压舌板

examples.en: Tom took a spatula out of the drawer.
examples.zh: 汤姆从抽屉里拿出一把锅铲。

examples.en: Unable to find a spatula, Tom used tongs to flip the pancakes.
examples.zh: 汤姆找不到锅铲了，只好用夹子为煎饼翻面。

examples.en: What did you do with the spatula?
examples.zh: 你把锅铲怎么处理了？

sergeant.definition: n. any of several noncommissioned officer ranks in the Army or Air Force or Marines ranking above a corporal
sergeant.translation: n. 警察小队长, 军士

examples.en: The old sergeant was not less moved than the captain.
Who goes there? shouted the sergeant in a hoarse voice.
The sergeant ordered the private to do push ups.

spinach.definition: n. southwestern Asian plant widely cultivated for its succulent edible dark green leaves\nn. dark green leaves; eaten cooked or raw in salads
spinach.translation: n. 菠菜, 货币, 胡说八道

examples.en: Tom didn't like spinach when he was a child.
examples.zh: 汤姆小时候不喜欢菠菜。

examples.en: I don't think that Tom likes spinach very much.
examples.zh: 我认为汤姆不太喜欢菠菜。

examples.en: I don't think Tom likes spinach very much.
examples.zh: 我认为汤姆不太喜欢菠菜。

seahorse.definition: n. small fish with horse-like heads bent sharply downward and curled tails; swim in upright position

examples.en: The seahorse is a unique animal.
The male seahorse carries the eggs.
In seahorses it's the male that gets pregnant.

stork.definition: n. large mostly Old World wading birds typically having white-and-black plumage

examples.en: Is that a stork or a heron?
examples.zh: 那是一只鹳还是一只苍鹭？

examples.en: Tom wasn't brought by the stork; he was found on a cabbage field.
examples.zh: 汤姆不是仙鹳带来的，而是在一片高丽菜田里被发现的。

swan.definition: n. stately heavy-bodied aquatic bird with very long neck and usually white plumage as adult\nv. sweep majestically
swan.translation: n. 天鹅, 天鹅星座, 有才华的诗人\nvi. 闲荡, 蜿蜒而行

examples.en: Gabriel watched a family of swans gliding gracefully on the lake.
examples.zh: 加布里埃尔看著一群天鹅在湖面上优雅地游著。

examples.en: This swan is black.
examples.zh: 这只天鹅是黑色的。

scream.definition: n. sharp piercing cry\nv. make a loud, piercing sound
scream.translation: n. 尖叫声\nvi. 尖叫, 大笑, 尖啸, 令人震惊\nvt. 尖叫着说, 大叫大嚷着要求

examples.en: There was a minute of silence and then everybody started screaming.
examples.zh: 有一分钟的沉默，然后每个人都开始尖叫。

examples.en: This time, it was James who screamed.
examples.zh: 这次换詹姆斯尖叫了。

examples.en: The wind sounds scary, like screaming ghosts.
examples.zh: 风声有点恐怖，听起来好像鬼叫一般。

supplier.definition: n. someone whose business is to supply a particular service or commodity
supplier.translation: n. 供应者, 供给国, 供应商\n[化] 承制厂; 供应厂商

examples.en: We want to develop a new supply chain with a supplier from Algeria.
examples.zh: 我们想和一个阿尔及利亚的供应商一起打造一条新的供应链。

sacrificial.definition: a. used in or connected with a sacrifice
sacrificial.translation: a. 牺牲的, 献祭的, 亏本的

examples.en: How many sacrificial lambs do we need to bring the rain back?
They turned me into a sacrificial sheep.

salvage.definition:
n. property or goods saved from damage or destruction
n. the act of saving goods or property that were in danger of damage or destruction
n. the act of rescuing a ship or its crew or its cargo from a shipwreck or a fire
v. save from ruin, destruction, or harm
salvage.translation: n. 海上救助, 抢救, 打捞, 抢救出来的财物\nvt. 海上救助, 抢救, 打捞, 营救\n[计] 文件恢复程序

examples.en: The wreckage of the ship was salvaged after it had gone to Davy Jones's locker.
examples.zh: 船的残骸从海底被打捞上来。

sanitation.definition: n. the state of being clean and conducive to health\nn. making something sanitary (free of germs) as by sterilizing
sanitation.translation: n. (环境)卫生, 环境卫生的提倡/维持, 卫生设备, 下水道设施, 卫生设施\n[医] 环境卫生

examples.en: Algerian sanitation workers have their work cut out for them.
Poor sanitation practices rendered Europe helpless against the Black Death.
Without water, sanitation and hygiene standards in the hospitals deteriorate.

sarcasm.definition: n. witty language used to convey insults or scorn
sarcasm.translation: n. 挖苦, 讽刺, 讽刺话, 讽刺性

examples.en: Do I detect a hint of sarcasm in your reply?
He spoke with a suggestion of sarcasm in his voice.
She spoke with a suggestion of sarcasm in her voice.

sarcastic.definition: a. expressing or expressive of ridicule that wounds
sarcastic.translation: a. 讽刺的, 讥讽的

examples.en: Don't you think the name "The Sacred War" sounds a bit sarcastic?
examples.zh: 你不觉得这个名字很讽刺吗，「神圣的战争」？

examples.en: Tom is quite sarcastic.
examples.zh: 汤姆真会挖苦人。

satire.definition: n witty language used to convey insults or scorn
satire.translation: n. 讽刺文学, 讽刺

examples.en: Our world must be a satire of some other world.
The play is a satire on the political world.
He was not aware that the praise was a satire in disguise.

satirical.definition: s. exposing human folly to ridicule
satirical.translation: a. 讽刺的, 讥讽的, 好挖苦的, 写讽刺作品的

examples.en: Charlie Hebdo is a satirical, secular, political, and cheerful newspaper.
I find satirical comedy to be the most amusing.
"Gulf of America" was a satirical name in the early 2010s.

satirist.definition: n. a humorist who uses ridicule and irony and sarcasm
satirist.translation: n. 讽刺作者, 爱挖苦的人

satisfactory.translation: a. 满意的, 赎罪的\n[法] 令人满意的, 令当事人满意的, 充分的

examples.en: The results of the research were quite satisfactory.
examples.zh: 调查的结果十分令人满意。

examples.en: The explanation is by no means satisfactory.
examples.zh: 这个解释不是很令人满意。

scholastic.definition: n. a Scholastic philosopher or theologian\na. of or relating to schools\na. of or relating to the philosophical doctrine of scholasticism
scholastic.translation: a. 学校的, 学校教育的, 学者的, 学究的\nn. 经院哲学家, 学究, 墨守成规者, 学生

examples.en: With Renaissance, scholastic ideas gave place to positive ideas.
examples.zh: 随著文艺复兴，学院派的想法被积极的想法取而代之了。

scrutinize.definition: v to look at critically or searchingly, or in minute detail\nv examine carefully for accuracy with the intent of verification
scrutinize.translation: vt.vi. 细看, 仔细检查, 审查, 细阅\n[法] 细看, 细阅, 仔细检查

examples.en: He scrutinized the document one final time before approving it.
He was carefully scrutinizing the man sitting in front of him.
Spenser's mother often scrutinizes him for every small mistake he makes.

secrecy.definition: n. the trait of keeping things secret
secrecy.translation: n. 秘密, 保密\n[法] 秘密, 秘密状态, 保密

examples.en: This plan requires secrecy.
examples.zh: 这个计划必须保持秘密。

seduce.definition: v. induce to have sex\nv. lure or entice away from duty, principles, or proper conduct
seduce.translation: vt. 唆使, 怂恿, 引诱, 诱奸\n[法] 勾引, 诱惑, 诱奸

examples.en: He seduced her with his didgeridoo.
examples.zh: 他用他的迪吉里杜管勾引了她。

seduction.definition: n. enticing someone astray from right behavior\nn. an act of winning the love or sexual favor of someone
seduction.translation: n. 教唆, 怂恿, 诱惑, 诱惑物, 诱饵\n[法] 诱奸, 勾引, 引诱

examples.en: Sami entered a new world of seduction and sex.
To achieve his ends, he resorts to seduction.
To achieve her ends, she resorts to seduction.

seductive.definition: a. tending to entice into a desired action or state
seductive.translation: a. 诱惑的, 引人注意的, 有魅力的

examples.en: A brilliant, seductive chef turns to espionage in Napoleon-era France.
examples.zh: 拿破仑时代的法国，魅力诱人的天才厨师摇身一变成为间谍。

seedling.definition: n. young plant or tree grown from a seed
seedling.translation: n. 秧苗, 树苗\n[医] 籽苗, 幼苗, 实生苗

examples.en: These seedlings are ready to be planted in the garden.
At the foot of the palm tree there grows a palm seedling.
Spread compost on the garden beds before planting your seedlings.

seeming.definition:
v give a certain impression or have a certain outward aspect
v seem to be true, probable, or apparent
v appear to exist
v appear to one's own mind or opinion
s appearing as such but not necessarily so
seeming.translation: a. 表面上的\nn. 外观

examples.en: They seem to have had a good time in Rome.
examples.zh: 他们看来在罗马过了些好日子。

examples.en: It doesn't seem very fair to treat him like this.
examples.zh: 这样对待他似乎不太公平。

examples.en: You seem to have mistaken me for my elder brother.
examples.zh: 你似乎把我当成我哥哥了。

segregate.definition: n. someone who is or has been segregated\nv. separate by race or religion; practice a policy of racial segregation\nv. divide from the main body or mass and collect
segregate.translation: a. 分离的, 被隔离的\nvi. 分离, 隔离, 分凝\nvt. 使分离, 使隔离

examples.en: People often segregate the two approaches, but they can often work together.
Racist politicians want to segregate schools again.
Yanni lives a segregated life in a lofty villa in Algiers.

segregation.definition: n. (genetics) the separation of paired alleles during meiosis so that members of each pair of alleles appear in different gametes\nn. a social system that provides separate facilities for minority groups\nn. the act of segregating or sequestering
segregation.translation: n. 隔离, 偏析, 被隔离的部分, 种族隔离\n[化] 分离; 分凝; 离析; 偏析; 分聚

examples.en: I don't agree with segregation of people by race.
The masses are entirely ignorant of the segregation problem.
Segregation of employees on the grounds of race is also unlawful.

seizure.definition: n. a sudden occurrence (or recurrence) of a disease\nn. the taking possession of something by legal process
seizure.translation: n. 捕获, 夺取, 占领, 捕获物, 没收, 充公\n[医] 发作; 癫痫发作

examples.en: Have you ever been diagnosed with a seizure disorder?
Tom knows what to do when Mary has an epileptic seizure.
Yanni had a massive seizure in the mosque.

sequential.definition: s in regular succession without gaps
sequential.translation: a. 继续的, 后果的\n[计] 顺序的

examples.en: Will there be a sequential translation into other languages?
What is the sequential rule?
The team of researchers recorded the springtime soundscape of northern Alaska for five sequential years.

serving.definition:
n an individual quantity of food or drink taken as part of a meal
n the act of delivering a writ or summons upon someone
v serve a purpose, role, or function
v do duty or hold offices; serve in a specific function
v contribute or conduce to
v be used by; as of a utility
v help to some food; help with food or drink
v provide (usually but not necessarily food)
v devote (part of) one's life or efforts to, as of countries, institutions, or ideas
v promote, benefit, or be useful or beneficial to
v spend time in prison or in a labor camp
v work for or be a servant to
v deliver a warrant or summons to someone
v be sufficient; be adequate, either in quality or quantity
v do military service
v mate with
v put the ball into play
serving.translation: n. 服务, 招待, 上菜, 一份食物

examples.en: Tom is serving a life sentence.
examples.zh: 汤姆正在服无期徒刑。

examples.en: His son is serving his sentence.
examples.zh: 他的儿子正在服役。

examples.en: Sami and Layla were serving shots.
examples.zh: 萨米和莱拉正在发球。

shady.translation: a. 荫凉的, 成荫的, 阴暗的, 隐蔽的\n[法] 成问题的, 令人怀疑的

examples.en: Ivy is growing in the shady part of the house.
The seesaw was in a shady area of the playground.
You try to find something shady in whatever I say.

shaky.definition: s. vibrating slightly and irregularly; as e.g. with fear or cold or like the leaves of an aspen in a breeze
shaky.translation: a. 震动的, 摇晃的, 动摇的

examples.en: Your plan is standing on a very shaky base support.
Tom is on pretty shaky ground as it is.
Give me another ladder, this one is too shaky.

shipyard.definition: n. a workplace where ships are built or repaired
shipyard.translation: n. 造船厂\n[经] 船坞, 造船厂, 修船厂

examples.en: That ship was towed into the shipyard to undergo alterations.
Lech Wałęsa jumped over the shipyard fence in 1980.
That ship was towed into the shipyard for refitting.

shorthand.definition: n. a method of writing rapidly\ns. written in abbreviated or symbolic form
shorthand.translation: n. 速记\n[法] 速记法, 速记, 记录文字

examples.en: That girl couldn't take things down in longhand, let alone shorthand.
We become very shorthanded at the end of the year.
She took down the speech in shorthand.

showy.translation: a. 艳丽的, 炫耀的

examples.en: This showy dress isn't appropriate for me.
I have no cell phone, no showy photos, no funny personality. Just medicaments.
Yanni was showy with his cars.

shred.definition: n. a tiny or scarcely detectable amount\nv. tear into shreds
shred.translation: n. 碎布条, 细片, 少量\nv. 撕碎

examples.en: She shredded the lettuce.
examples.zh: 她把生菜切丝。

examples.en: Two women wielding giant spatulas continuously stir a brimming wok of shredded beef simmering in curry sauce.
examples.zh: 两名女子挥舞著巨大的锅铲，不停地翻炒著盛满咖哩酱汁的牛肉丝。

shrubbery.definition: n. an area where a number of shrubs are planted\nn. a collection of shrubs growing together

examples.en: We're all going to be eaten by a monstrous talking shrubbery.
A small wicket-gate opened upon a footpath that wound through some shrubbery to the door.

shyly.definition: r. in a shy or timid or bashful manner
shyly.translation: adv. 害羞地；羞怯地；胆怯地；小心地

examples.en: She glanced shyly at the young man.
examples.zh: 她羞怯地看了一眼那个年轻人。

examples.en: Dad looked at Mom shyly.
examples.zh: 爸爸害羞地看著妈妈。

sinister.definition: s. on or starting from the wearer's left
sinister.translation: a. 不吉利的, 凶恶的, 左边的\n[医] 左的

examples.en: Ziri had the most sinister evil face I've ever seen.
Yanni's eyes were deranged and he had a sinister smile.
There was something quite special, almost sinister to his smile.

sizable.definition: s fairly large\ns large in amount or extent or degree
sizable.translation: a. 相当大的, 大小相当的

examples.en: He received a sizable advance for his book.
A sizable portion of his students loved him.
Tom won a sizable amount of money.

sketchy.definition: s. giving only major points; lacking completeness
sketchy.translation: a. 概略的, 草草完成的

examples.en: Carlos came across as a little sketchy to Melissa.
While in the US, Lorenzo ran into a few sketchy areas.
His explanation was too sketchy. I didn't understand it.

skim.definition:
n. a thin layer covering the surface of a liquid
n. reading or glancing through quickly
v. cause to skip over a surface
v. coat (a liquid) with a layer
skim.translation:
vt. 撇取浮沫, 略读, 掠过
vi. 擦过, 浏览
n. 脱脂乳, 擦过, 表层物
a. 撇去浮沫的

examples.en: Let the milk stand overnight and skim off the cream.
Semi-skimmed milk has a fat level between whole and skim milk.
The plane quickly skimmed the surface of the calm sea.

slack.definition:
n. dust consisting of a mixture of small coal fragments and coal dust and dirt that sifts out when coal is passed over a sieve
n. a stretch of water without current or movement
n. the quality of being loose (not taut)
n. a cord or rope or cable that is hanging loosely
slack.translation:
n. 松弛, 松懈, 淡季, 闲散, 家常裤
a. 松弛的, 不流畅的, 疏忽的, 无力的, 呆滞的, 软弱的, 漏水的
adv. 马虎地, 缓慢地
vt. 放松, 使缓慢
vi. 松懈, 减弱, 松弛

examples.en: You are a big slacker.
examples.zh: 你是一个大懒鬼。

smelly.translation: a. 发臭的, 有臭味的

examples.en: Why did God decide to give us all smelly butts?
I had to use a dirty, smelly gas station bathroom.
Take off those smelly socks: they're soaking wet with sweat.

smuggler.definition: n. someone who imports or exports without paying duties
smuggler.translation: n. 走私者, 走私船\n[经] 走私者, 走私船

examples.en: The drug smuggler was arrested at the airport.
The townspeople were astonishingly naive about what the smugglers were.
I knew you were a smuggler.

smuggling.definition: n. secretly importing prohibited goods or goods on which duty is due

examples.en: The police arrested him for smuggling.
examples.zh: 警察以走私为由逮捕了他。

snob.definition: n. a person regarded as arrogant and annoying
snob.translation: n. 势利的人, 假内行

examples.en: Tom is a bit of a snob, isn't he?
Mary is a bit of a snob, isn't she?
Tom is a snob when it comes to wine.

snobbish.definition: s befitting or characteristic of those who incline to social exclusiveness and who rebuff the advances of people considered inferior
snobbish.translation: a. 自命不凡的, 势利的

examples.en: Tom is a bit snobbish.
examples.zh: 汤姆有一点势利。

sodium.definition: n. a silvery soft waxy metallic element of the alkali metal group; occurs abundantly in natural compounds (especially in salt water); burns with a yellow flame and reacts violently in water; occurs in sea water and in the mineral halite (rock salt)

examples.en: Sodium bicarbonate is commonly known as baking soda.
examples.zh: 碳酸氢钠通常被称为小苏打。

solicit.definition: v. make a solicitation or entreaty for something; request urgently or persistently\nv. incite, move, or persuade to some act of lawlessness or insubordination\nv. make a solicitation or petition for something desired
solicit.translation: v. 请求, 乞求, 招揽, 征求

examples.en: What is your reason for soliciting a conversation with me?
examples.zh: 你恳求与我谈话的原因是什么？

solidify.definition: v. make solid or more solid; cause to solidify\nv. become solid
solidify.translation: v. (使)凝固, (使)团结, 巩固

examples.en: Mary finds that discussing topics with Tom helps solidify her knowledge.
Basalt is a type of rock that forms when lava solidifies.
Islam solidified its place in the Sahara during the Middle Ages.

solitary.definition:
n confinement of a prisoner in isolation from other prisoners
n one who lives in solitude
s characterized by or preferring solitude
s of plants and animals; not growing or living in groups or colonies
s lacking companions or companionship
s being the only one; single and isolated from others
s devoid of creatures
solitary.translation: n. 独居者\na. 孤独的, 独居的

examples.en: I like a solitary walk.
examples.zh: 我喜欢一个人散步。

examples.en: Bears are solitary animals.
examples.zh: 熊是一种独居动物。

solitude.definition: n. a state of social isolation\nn. the state or situation of being alone\nn. a solitary place
solitude.translation: n. 孤独, 单独, 孤寂

examples.en: He likes to spend some time in solitude every day.
examples.zh: 他喜欢每天都享受一下一个人的时间。

soluble.definition: a. (of a substance) capable of being dissolved in some solvent (usually water)\na. susceptible of solution or of being solved or explained
soluble.translation: a. 溶解的, 可溶解的, 可以解决的\n[医] 溶解的, 可溶的

examples.en: Sugar is soluble in water.
examples.zh: 糖溶于水。

sophistication.definition: n. being expert or having knowledge of some technical subject\nn. the quality or character of being intellectually sophisticated and worldly through cultivation or experience or disillusionment\nn. falsification by the use of sophistry; misleading by means of specious fallacies
sophistication.translation: n. 诡辩, 老于世故, 复杂(性)\n[医] 掺假

examples.en: The black tie event had an air of sophistication.
The black leather couch added a touch of sophistication.
Automobile transmissions have grown in sophistication over the years.

sorrow.definition: n. an emotion of great sadness associated with loss or bereavement\nn. sadness associated with some wrong done or some disappointment
sorrow.translation: n. 悲伤, 哀惜, 不幸\nvi. 悲伤, 懊悔, 遗憾

examples.en: The loss of his mother brought him sorrow and regret.
examples.zh: 他母亲的离世带给他悲伤和遗憾。

examples.en: The death of languages leaves people feeling regret and sorrow.
examples.zh: 语言们的死亡令人遗憾而悲伤。

examples.en: His mother's passing brought him sorrow and regret.
examples.zh: 他母亲的离世带给他悲伤和遗憾。

sorrowful.definition: a. experiencing or marked by or expressing sorrow especially that associated with irreparable loss

examples.en: You know I am a bit sorrowful.
In hard times, in sorrowful times, let's try doing something for other people.
The ancient ones built the sorrowful lighthouses to guide their miserable wooden ships.

spear.definition:
n. a long pointed rod used as a tool or weapon
n. an implement with a shaft and barbed point used for catching fish
v. pierce with a spear
v. thrust up like a spear
spear.translation:
n. 矛, 枪, 持矛者, 嫩枝
vt. 用矛刺
vi. 刺, 戳
a. 父系的

examples.en: The tip of the spear was dipped in a deadly poison.
examples.zh: 矛尖浸在一种致命的毒药里。

examples.en: Where is Britney Spears?
examples.zh: 小甜甜布莱尼在哪里？

speeding.definition:
n changing location rapidly
v move fast
v move faster
v move very fast
v travel at an excessive or illegal velocity
v cause to move faster

examples.en: Sami's car suddenly veered off, speeding away.
examples.zh: 萨米的车突然转向，加速驶去。

examples.en: The driver was charged with speeding.
examples.zh: 司机被控超速驾驶。

examples.en: Ken was fined 7,000 yen for speeding.
examples.zh: 肯因超速被罚款7000日元。

speedy.definition: s characterized by speed; moving with or capable of moving with high speed\ns accomplished rapidly and without delay
speedy.translation: a. 快的, 迅速的\n[经] 快的, 迅速的

examples.en: I wish you a speedy recovery!
examples.zh: 祝你早日痊愈!

examples.en: I wish you a speedy recovery.
examples.zh: 祝你早日痊愈!

splendor.definition: n a quality that outshines the usual\nn the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand
splendor.translation: n. 光辉, 壮丽, 显赫

examples.en: The reason the Northern and Southern Dynasties had failed in their rule was that they allowed literary splendor to surpass real substance.
examples.zh: 南北朝在他们的统治之下失败了的原因是他们让文学的光辉超越了实质内容。

spokesperson.definition: n. an advocate who represents someone else's policy or purpose
spokesperson.translation: n. 发言人, 代言人

examples.en: Do you want to be the spokesperson of our group?
She seems oddly shy and retiring for a media spokesperson.
I'm delighted to have Mennad as my new spokesperson.

spokeswoman.translation: n. 女发言人, 女代言人

examples.en: The high commissioner’s spokeswoman said the government had shown some willingness to initiate reforms.
State police spokeswoman Janet Welp says the truck wound up crashing into a bridge railing along Interstate 30.
The spokeswoman for the International Organization for Migration says the migrants are living under very flimsy, open structures.

spongy.definition: s. easily squashed; resembling a sponge in having soft porous texture and compressibility\ns. like a sponge in being able to absorb liquids and yield it back when compressed
spongy.translation: a. 海绵状的, 海绵质的, 多孔的\n[医] 海绵状的, 海绵构造的

examples.en: Oooh, sick! What is that stuff? It's all spongy.
Oooh, gross! What is that stuff? It's all spongy.
The ground is spongy.

sponsorship.definition: n. the act of sponsoring (either officially or financially)
sponsorship.translation: n. 发起, 倡议, 主办, 保证人的地位, 教父的地位, 教母的地位

examples.en: According to Rafael Leitão, it is very difficult for a professional chess player to get sponsorship in Brazil, because chess is not popular in our country.
examples.zh: 拉斐尔莱唐表示，在巴西，职业棋手很难获得赞助，因为西洋棋在巴西并不流行。

spontaneity.definition: n. the quality of being spontaneous and coming from natural feelings without constraint
spontaneity.translation: n. 自然发生, 自生, 自发

examples.en: Your desire for order clashes with my appreciation for spontaneity.
Her spontaneity borders on stupidity.
Her spontaneity bordered on stupidity.

sportsman.definition: n someone who engages in sports
sportsman.translation: n. 运动员, 冒险家

examples.en: He looks like a sportsman, but he is a writer.
examples.zh: 他看起来像个运动员，但是其实是个作家。

sportswoman.definition: n someone who engages in sports

examples.en: Eva realised her dream of becoming a prominent sportswoman in the Olympics.

sprawl.definition: n. an ungainly posture with arms and legs spread about\nv. sit or lie with one's limbs spread out\nv. go, come, or spread in a rambling or irregular way
sprawl.translation: vi. 伸开手足躺, 爬行, 蔓生, 蔓延\nvt. 懒散地伸开, 使蔓生, 使不规则地伸展\nn. 伸开手足躺卧姿势

examples.en: Urban sprawl is environmentally damaging.
examples.zh: 城市扩张会对环境造成破坏。

stagnate.definition: v. stand still\nv. cause to stagnate\nv. cease to flow; stand without moving
stagnate.translation: v. (使)淤塞, (使)停滞, (使)变萧条

examples.en: The project began to stagnate without effective leadership.
The country stagnated economically for the next half century.
When economic growth stagnates or even declines, debts cannot be reduced.

stagnation.definition: n. a state of inactivity (in business or art etc)\nn. inactivity of liquids; being stagnant; standing still; without current or circulation
stagnation.translation: n. 淤塞, 停滞\n[医] 停滞, 滞留, 郁积

examples.en: What are the reasons of the stagnation of Algeria's economy?
Is the Algerian economy doomed to stagnation?
Don't fear slow progress, only stagnation.

stammer.definition: n. a speech disorder involving hesitations and involuntary repetitions of certain sounds
stammer.translation: v. 口吃, 结结巴巴地说\nn. 口吃, 结巴

examples.en: When suddenly asked a question, I often stammer to respond.
Please do not mock me for my stammer.
The new boy had a nervous stammer.

stark.translation: a. 僵硬的, 完全的, 刻板的, 明显的, 荒凉的, 结实的\nadv. 突出地, 简直, 全然

examples.en: My little brother ran through the living room stark naked.
examples.zh: 我弟弟全身光溜溜地跑过客厅。

stationery.definition: n. paper cut to an appropriate size for writing letters; usually with matching envelopes
stationery.translation: n. 文具, 信纸\n[法] 文具

examples.en: All of this stationery is his.
examples.zh: 这些都是他的文具。

examples.en: What stationery isn't worth buying?
examples.zh: 哪些文具不值得买？

statistic.definition: n. a datum that can be represented numerically
statistic.translation: n. 统计量\na. 统计的, 统计学的

examples.en: If you think about, everyone is already a statistic.
One death is a tragedy. A million deaths is a statistic.
Factory production — the largest component of the statistic — jumped by 0.7 percent.

statutory.definition: a. relating to or created by statutes\ns. prescribed or authorized by or punishable under a statute
statutory.translation: a. 法令的, 法定的, 可依法惩处的\n[经] 法定的

examples.en: Statutory law is written and passed by a legislature.
Her father was accused of statutory rape.
There are no statutory minimum paid vacations or paid public holidays in the United States.

steamy.definition: s filled with steam or emitting moisture in the form of vapor or mist\ns hot or warm and humid\ns feeling great sexual desire
steamy.translation: a. 蒸汽的, 充满蒸汽的

examples.en: Sami was involved in a steamy affair with Layla.
Sami has been having a steamy affair with Layla.
Yanni was having a steamy affair with Ziri's wife.

stewardess.definition: n. a woman steward on an airplane
stewardess.translation: n. 空中小姐, 女管理人, 女管家

examples.en: Jane was a stewardess when she was young.
examples.zh: Jane 年轻时曾做过女乘务员。

examples.en: A stewardess was rescued from the wreck.
examples.zh: 一名空姐从飞机残骸中被救出来了。

examples.en: He married a stewardess.
examples.zh: 他娶了一位空姐。

stifle.definition: n. joint between the femur and tibia in a quadruped; corresponds to the human knee\nv. smother or suppress
stifle.translation: vt. 使窒息, 抑止, 扼杀\nvi. 窒息, 被扼杀

examples.en: I had to stifle my anger in front of him.
Sami stuffed a bag inside Layla's mouth to stifle her.
Why do you stifle me so by complaining?

stimulant.definition: n. a drug that temporarily quickens some vital process\ns. that stimulates
stimulant.translation: a. 兴奋性的, 激励的, 鼓舞的\nn. 兴奋剂, 酒精饮料

examples.en: Ecstasy is a stimulant type of drug.
Ivan injected Rima with a stimulant.
Intoxication is what happens when the brain is affected by certain stimulants.

stoop.definition:
n. an inclination of the top half of the body forward and downward
n. small porch or set of steps at the front entrance of a house
v. descend swiftly, as if on prey
v. sag, bend, bend over or down
stoop.translation: n. 佝偻, 屈从, 弯腰\nvi. 弯下, 屈从, 弯腰, 堕落\nvt. 使屈从, 使弯曲

examples.en: She stooped to pick up a pebble.
examples.zh: 她捡起了一块鹅卵石。

stoppage.definition: n the state of inactivity following an interruption\nn an obstruction in a pipe or tube\nn the act of stopping something
stoppage.translation: n. 停止, 中止, 阻塞, 阻碍, 堵塞, 故障, 停付, 扣除, 扣留, 停工, 罢工\n[化] 停机

examples.en: A soccer match lasts 90 minutes, without considering stoppage time.
There's a difference in the duration of a football match between normal time and stoppage time.

strangle.definition: v. kill by squeezing the throat of so as to cut off the air\nv. die from strangulation
strangle.translation: vt. 勒死, 扼死, 压制, 使窒息, 抑制\nvi. 被扼死, 被绞死, 窒息而死

examples.en: Tom leaped at Mary and tried to strangle her.
Sami used his bare hands to strangle his wife.
Dan slipped into Linda's hospital room and tried to strangle her.

stuffy.definition: s. affected with a sensation of stoppage or obstruction
stuffy.translation: a. 闷热的, 窒息的, 乏味的, 固步自封的, 自以为是的

examples.en: It's very stuffy in here. Can we open a window?
It's so stuffy in here. Can someone open a window?
It's so stuffy in here. Could someone open a window?

stunning.definition: s. causing great astonishment and consternation\ns. causing or capable of causing bewilderment or shock or insensibility\ns. strikingly beautiful or attractive
stunning.translation: a. 打昏迷的, 弄得人昏头昏脑的, 令人震惊的

examples.en: Thousands of laborers and craftsmen toiled for 22 years to craft the stunning white marble edifice.
examples.zh: 数千名工人和工匠辛勤工作了 22 年，才打造出这座令人惊叹的白色大理石建筑。

examples.en: They're creating stunning works of art to force people to stop and appreciate the beauty of the universe.
examples.zh: 他们创作出令人惊叹的艺术作品，从而让人们驻足欣赏宇宙之美。

stylish.definition: a. having elegance or taste or refinement in manners or dress
stylish.translation: a. 现代风格的, 流行的, 潇洒的

examples.en: This is not very stylish.
examples.zh: 这不是很流行。

submerge.definition: v. sink below the surface; go under or as if under water\nv. cover completely or make imperceptible\nv. put under water
submerge.translation: vt. 使浸水, 使陷入, 淹没\nvi. 潜入水中

examples.en: Due to global warming, cities could be completely submerged.
examples.zh: 由于全球气候变暖，城市可能被完全地淹没。

examples.en: People living on coastlines might lose their homes, and cities might be completely submerged.
examples.zh: 住在海边的人可能失去他们的家，并且城市可能会被完全淹没。

examples.en: I want to submerge myself in the ocean depths, and to disappear there so as to never be seen again.
examples.zh: 我想沉到海里去，在这个世界上消失，这样就不会再有人看见我了。

submissive.definition: a. inclined or willing to submit to orders or wishes of others or showing such inclination
submissive.translation: a. 服从的, 顺从的

examples.en: Dominant or submissive - which part do you want to play?
Mary's energetic vigor mixed surprisingly well with Tom's submissive eagerness.
Jake, a dominant, advertised for a compatible submissive online.

subsidize.definition: v. support through subsidies\nv. secure the assistance of by granting a subsidy, as of nations or military forces
subsidize.translation: vt. 补助, 资助, 贿赂\n[经] 资助, 津贴, 给...补助金

examples.en: The city should subsidize small businesses in industries with large overhead costs.
examples.zh: 市府应补贴经常性开支庞大的产业中的小型企业。

subsistence.definition: n. minimal (or marginal) resources for subsisting\nn. a means of surviving\nn. the state of existing in reality; having substance
subsistence.translation: n. 生存, 生活\n[医] 生存

examples.en: Agriculture provides a subsistence livelihood for 85% of the people.
That is a necessary contribution to its subsistence.
Subsistence farming is the dominant form of livelihood.

substitution.definition: n. an event in which one thing is substituted for another\nn. the act of putting one thing or person in the place of another: "he sent Smith in for Jones but the substitution came too late to help"
substitution.translation: n. 代替, 替换, 代替物\n[计] 置换

examples.en: There is a widespread opinion that all study of the mode of oratory is unmanly, and leads to the substitution of artifice and adornment for simplicity and power.
examples.zh: 有一种普遍的看法认为，一切对演说方式的研究都是有损男子气概的，都会以雕饰与浮华取代质朴与力量。

subtlety.definition: n. the quality of being difficult to detect or analyze

examples.en: Subtlety has never been your strong suit.
Subtlety never was her strong suit.
Subtlety never was your strong suit.

subtract.definition: v. make a subtraction\nv. take off or away
subtract.translation: vt. 减去, 扣掉, 减少\nvi. 做减法\n[计] 减

examples.en: Subtract two from ten and you have eight.
examples.zh: 十减二等于八。

examples.en: Subtract three from eight and you get five.
examples.zh: 八减去三就能得到五。

subtraction.definition: n. an arithmetic operation in which the difference between two numbers is calculated\nn. the act of subtracting (removing a part from the whole)

examples.en: There is only one arithmetic operation inherent in war: subtraction.
Do you know the difference between addition, subtraction, and multiplication?
The addition is correct, but there is an error in your subtraction.

superstitious.definition: s. showing ignorance of the laws of nature and faith in magic or chance
superstitious.translation: a. 迷信的\n[法] 迷信的, 由迷信引起的

examples.en: I didn't know that you were such a superstitious person.
I'm not superstitious, but that was a black cat.
I'm not brave, I admit; but I'm not superstitious.

supplementary.definition: s. added to complete or make up a deficiency
supplementary.translation: a. 补足的, 补充的, 追加的\n[经] 追加的, 补充的, 增补的

examples.en: Supplementary information includes adverbs and things that function as adverbs.
You may need a supplementary dose after six months.

supposition.definition: n. the cognitive process of supposing
supposition.translation: n. 想像, 推测, 推想\n[法] 假定, 推定, 推测

examples.en: It is founded on supposition.
examples.zh: 这是建立在猜测的基础上。

suppression.definition: n. the failure to develop some part or organ\nn. the act of withholding or withdrawing some book or writing from publication or circulation\nn. forceful prevention; putting down by power or authority
suppression.translation: n. 抑压, 镇压, 抑制\n[计] 抑制

examples.en: A caged bird represents a suppression of some urge or drive.
Suppression and distortion of historical facts are unacceptable.
The biggest threat to democracy in the United States is voter suppression.

surf.definition: n. waves breaking on the shore\nv. switch channels, on television
surf.translation: n. 海浪, 拍岸浪\nvi. 作冲浪运动

examples.en: She spends way too much time surfing the web.
examples.zh: 她花实在太多的时间在网上冲浪。

examples.en: Why do you go online, surf, chat, and use QQ every time you have free time, wasting an entire night on it?
examples.zh: 你怎么一有空就上网，冲浪灌水打QQ，一个夜晚就扔给它了？

surname.definition: n. the name used to identify the members of a family (as distinguished from each member's given name)
surname.translation: n. 姓, 别号, 绰号\nvt. 呼以姓氏, 起绰号

examples.en: The surname Wang is the most common in China.
examples.zh: 中国姓王的人最多。

examples.en: In France, the first name goes before the surname.
examples.zh: 在法国，名放在姓前面。

examples.en: In France the first name comes before the surname.
examples.zh: 在法国，名放在姓前面。

surpass.definition: v. be or do something to a greater degree
surpass.translation: vt. 超越, 凌驾, 胜过

examples.en: However, other aspects have already surpassed the standards of many Western countries.
examples.zh: 不过，其它的方面已经超过了很多西方国家的程度。

examples.en: He surpasses his rivals in all ways.
examples.zh: 他在各方面都超出他的对手。

examples.en: No one surpasses him.
examples.zh: 没人能超过他。

surroundings.definition:
n the environmental condition
n the area in which something exists or lives
v extend on all sides of simultaneously; encircle
v envelop completely
v surround so as to force to give up
v surround with a wall in order to fortify
surroundings.translation: n. 环境, 周围的事物\n[化] 环境

examples.en: The rescuers searched the surroundings in hopes of finding the child.
examples.zh: 援救人员为了找到孩子，仔细搜索了那个区域。

examples.en: He soon got used to the new surroundings.
examples.zh: 他很快就适应了新的环境。

examples.en: No sign of the enemy in our surroundings.
examples.zh: 在我们的周围没有敌人的迹象。

sustainability.definition: n. the property of being sustainable
sustainability.translation: n. 持续性, 能维持性, 永续性

examples.en: Mary's garden is a blend of beauty and sustainability.
What can we learn from other cultures about sustainability?
Sustainability is part of our responsibility as software engineers.

sway.translation: n. 摇摆, 影响力, 支配\nvt. 摇动, 支配, 弄歪, 使倾斜, 使动摇, 影响\nvi. 摇动, 摇摆, 倾斜, 动摇, 统治, 转向

examples.en: From the time he got up, his beliefs began to sway.
examples.zh: 从那时起，他的信仰开始摇动了。

examples.en: The willow branches swayed gently in the breeze.
examples.zh: 柳枝在微风中轻轻荡悠。

swipe.definition: n. a sweeping stroke or blow\nv. strike with a swiping motion
swipe.translation: n. 强打, 用力挥击, 尖刻的话, 碰擦, 起重杆\nvt. 强打, 用力挥击, 偷

examples.en: I already swiped the card.
examples.zh: 我已经刷卡了。

symmetric.definition: a having similarity in size, shape, and relative position of corresponding parts
symmetric.translation: a. 对称的, 均匀的, 匀称的\n[计] 对称的

examples.en: The relationship "A loves B" is not reflexive, transitive, or symmetric.

symphony.definition: n. a long and complex sonata for symphony orchestra
symphony.translation: n. 交响乐, 交响曲

examples.en: Do you know the concert schedule of London Symphony Orchestra?
examples.zh: 你知道伦敦交响乐团的演奏会行程吗？

syndicate.definition:
n. a loose affiliation of gangsters in charge of organized criminal activities
n. a news agency that sells features or articles or photographs etc. to newspapers for simultaneous publication
v. join together into a syndicate
v. organize into or form a syndicate
syndicate.translation: n. 企业联合, 辛迪加, 财团\nv. 联合成辛迪加

examples.en: The prize was divided equally among the ten syndicate members.
Boris was the leader of a local mafia syndicate.
Sami was involved in a drug syndicate.

synonym.definition: n. two words that can be interchanged in a context are said to be synonymous relative to that context

examples.en: The word ‘antonym’ is antonymous to ‘synonym’.
examples.zh: 反义词这个单词是同义词的反义词

synthesize.definition: v. combine so as to form a more complex, product\nv. combine and form a synthesis

examples.en: The lab is trying to synthesize an antidote to treat the poisoning victims.
Adrenochrome is not psychoactive and is easily synthesized.
How do you synthesize aspirin?

scar.definition: n. a mark left (usually on the skin) by the healing of injured tissue\nv. mark with a scar
scar.translation: n. 疤痕, 伤痕, 悬崖\nvi. 结疤, 愈合, 痊愈\nvt. 使有伤痕

examples.en: I'll still have a scar from that accident.
examples.zh: 我还留着那起事故的伤疤。

examples.en: The scar on his forehead really stands out.
examples.zh: 他额头上的疤痕很醒目。

examples.en: Tom has a scar on his cheek.
examples.zh: 汤姆的脸颊上有一块伤痕。

scarcity.definition: n. a small and inadequate amount
scarcity.translation: n. 缺乏, 不足, 缺少\n[经] 缺乏, 不足

examples.en: Gorelick said that the outcomes of his work in Jordan may be used to evaluate water scarcity in other Middle Eastern countries, such as Syria.
examples.zh: 戈雷利克表示，他在约旦的研究成果可用于评估叙利亚等其他中东国家的水资源短缺。

second-hand.translation: a. 用过的, 旧货的, 旧的, 间接的, 传来的, 第二手的\n[机] 半新的, 旧货

examples.en: Wearing second-hand clothes is now popular among young people.
examples.zh: 二手服饰在时下年轻人之间蔚为风潮。

shake.definition:
v. move or cause to move back and forth
v. move with or as if with a tremor
v. undermine or cause to waver
v. get rid of
shake.translation: n. 摇动, 震动\nvt. 摇动, 动摇, 使震动, 挥舞\nvi. 震动, 发抖, 动摇

examples.en: My hands were shaking too much to thread the needle.
examples.zh: 我的手抖得太厉害，没法穿针了。

examples.en: We felt the house shake a little.
examples.zh: 我们感觉到房子摇动了一下。

examples.en: He refused to shake hands with me.
examples.zh: 他拒绝跟我握手。

shave.definition:
n. the act of removing hair with a razor
v. remove body hair with a razor
v. cut closely
v. cut the price of
shave.translation: n. 修面, 刮胡子, 幸免, 剃刀\nvt. 修面, 剃, 修剪, 掠过\nvi. 刮脸, 勉强通过

examples.en: It is pleasant to shave off my beard.
examples.zh: 刮完胡子感觉很舒服。

examples.en: I got a shave and a haircut.
examples.zh: 我刮了胡子并理了发。

examples.en: A barber is a man who shaves and cuts men's hair.
examples.zh: 理发师是为男人刮胡子和剪头发的人。

sidewalk.definition: n. walk consisting of a paved area for pedestrians; usually beside a street or roadway

examples.en: I saw Tom pushing a stroller down the sidewalk.
examples.zh: 我看到汤姆推著婴儿车走在人行道上。

examples.en: I found a coin on the sidewalk.
examples.zh: 我在人行道上发现了一枚硬币。

examples.en: Tom is sweeping the sidewalk.
examples.zh: 汤姆正在清扫人行道。

sightseeing.definition: n. going about to look at places of interest
sightseeing.translation: n. 观光, 游览\na. 观光的, 游览的

examples.en: The sightseeing bus ran through a long tunnel.
examples.zh: 观光巴士穿过了一条长长的隧道。

sign.definition:
n. a perceptible indication of something not immediately apparent (as a visible clue that something has happened)
n. a public display of a message
n. (medicine) any objective evidence of the presence of a disorder or disease
n. a gesture that is part of a sign language
sign.translation:
n. 符号, 招牌, 征兆, 正负号, 手势
vt. 签名, 打手势表达
vi. 签名
[计] 正负号; 符号; 符号字符

examples.en: All you have to do is sign your name here.
examples.zh: 你在这里签个名就行了。

examples.en: Red, as opposed to green, is a sign of danger.
examples.zh: 红色，相对于绿色，是危险的标志。

examples.en: You must look over the contract before you sign it.
examples.zh: 你在签字前必须仔细看合同。

signpost.definition: n. a post bearing a sign that gives directions or shows the way\nv. mark with a signpost, as of a path
signpost.translation: n. 招牌柱, 广告柱, 路标

examples.en: The signpost had a green arrow pointing towards the park.
A poster was stapled onto a signpost.
Do you see that signpost there?

sloth.definition: n. a disinclination to work or exert yourself\nn. any of several slow-moving arboreal mammals of South America and Central America; they hang from branches back downward and feed on leaves and fruits\nn. apathy and inactivity in the practice of virtue (personified as one of the deadly sins)

examples.en: A sloth can live in the same tree for years.
And I'll be a chicken that smells like a sloth!
The sloth rests and sleeps for much of the day.

sought.definition: a. that is looked for\ns. being searched for

examples.en: He sought shelter from the rain.
examples.zh: 他四处寻找避雨的地方。

examples.en: People eagerly sought a more modernised style of dress and transformed the old qipao to suit their tastes.
examples.zh: 人们热切地寻求更有现代风格的衣服，所以把以前的旗袍改成了适合他们品位的东西。

examples.en: People could not see any hopes of obtaining happiness in this life, thus they instinctively sought comfort in the afterlife.
examples.zh: 人们在此世中看不到任何获得幸福的希望，便很本能地想在彼世中寻求慰藉。

souvenir.definition: n something of sentimental value\nn a reminder of past events

examples.en: What souvenir do you think she would like most?
examples.zh: 你觉得她最想要什么纪念品？

examples.en: Is there a souvenir shop in the hotel?
examples.zh: 旅馆里面有纪念品商店吗?

examples.en: Last week, I mailed him some souvenirs from the U.S.
examples.zh: 上周我寄了一些美国纪念品给他。

special.definition:
n. a special offering (usually temporary and at a reduced price) that is featured in advertising
n. a dish or meal given prominence in e.g. a restaurant
n. a television production that features a particular person or work or topic
s. for a special service or occasion
special.translation: n. 专辑, 专车, 号外, 特别的东西, 负有特别任务的人员\na. 特别的, 专门的, 特殊的, 额外的, 附加的, 特别亲密的

examples.en: This year is definitely a special year in human history.
examples.zh: 今年肯定是人类历史上特殊的一年。

examples.en: Your initial order is subject to a special discount of 5%.
examples.zh: 首次订购可获九五折的特别优惠。

examples.en: Sir, that CD is available only by special order.
examples.zh: 先生，那盘CD需要预定才有。

speck.definition: n. a very small spot\nv. produce specks in or on
speck.translation: n. 斑点, 有斑点的东西, 污点, 缺点, 微粒, 肥肉\nvt. 使有斑点

examples.en: There wasn't even a speck of dust on the table.
We're all just a speck of dust in the universe.
This world is a mere speck of dust.

spot.definition:
n. a short section or illustration (as between radio or tv programs or in a magazine) that is often used for advertising
n. a small contrasting part of something
n. a section of an entertainment that is assigned to a specific performer or performance
n. a business establishment for entertainment
spot.translation:
n. 污点, 地点, 斑点, 点, 娱乐场所, 处境, 少量
a. 当场的, 现场的, 现货买卖的, 现金交易的, 抽样的
vt. 点缀, 玷污, 认出, 准确定...的位, 用灯光照射
vi. 玷污, (从空中)侦察敌方目标

examples.en: He wants to go the library and get a spot.
examples.zh: 他要去图书馆占位。

examples.en: There were ten police officers on the spot.
examples.zh: 现场有10名警员。

examples.en: Algeria should become China's main investment hot spot in the Mediterranean region.
examples.zh: 阿尔及利亚应该成为中国在地中海地区的主要投资热点。

sprout.definition: n. any new growth of a plant such as a new branch or a bud\nn. a newly grown bud (especially from a germinating seed)\nv. put forth and grow sprouts or shoots
sprout.translation: n. 芽, 萌芽\nvt. 使发芽, 摘去芽\nvi. 长芽, 抽条

examples.en: The grass sprouts all over the garden.
examples.zh: 花园里的草发芽了。

examples.en: Organic kale is hand picked, washed and packed on site at Sprouting Farms, West Virginia, for retail and wholesale.
examples.zh: 有机羽衣甘蓝在西维吉尼亚州的 Sprouting Farms 现场手工采摘、清洗和包装，提供零售和批发。

stash.definition: n a secret store of valuables or money\nv save up as for future use
stash.translation: vt. 藏起来\nn. 隐藏处, 隐藏物

examples.en: Algerian police found a stash of weapons on that farm.
I have a secret stash of guacamole hidden in the fridge.
Where do you keep your stash of books?

static.definition: n. a crackling or hissing noise caused by electrical interference\nn. angry criticism\ns. showing little if any change
static.translation: n. 静电, 静电干扰\na. 静态的, 静止的, 固有的, 静电的

examples.en: You can't access an instance variable from a static method.
The static electricity started to make our hair stand on end.
House prices have remained static for several months.

stink.definition: v. be extremely bad in quality or in one's performance
stink.translation: n. 臭味, 臭气\nvi. 发臭味, 名声臭\nvt. 用臭味赶

examples.en: No, you don't stink.
examples.zh: 不是的，你不臭。

examples.en: These dirty socks stink.
examples.zh: 这脏袜子臭哄哄。

examples.en: Nail polish remover stinks a lot.
examples.zh: 洗甲水的味道很难闻。

stoke.definition: v. stir up or tend; of a fire

examples.en: Suddenly smelling smoke could be a sign of stoke.
I held her hand and stoked it with my thumb.
I asked Tom to stoke the fire.

straight.definition:
n. a poker hand with 5 consecutive cards (regardless of suit)
s. successive (without a break)
a. having no deviations
a. (of hair) having no waves or curls
straight.translation: n. 直线, 直\na. 直的, 笔直的, 正直的, 直接的, 连续的, 整齐的\nadv. 直接地, 立即, 不断地

examples.en: I recognised her straight away; she hasn't changed a bit.
examples.zh: 我一下子就认出她了，她一点儿都没变。

examples.en: Go straight on to the end of the road.
examples.zh: 直走直到这条街道的尽头。

examples.en: He was ill in bed for four days straight.
examples.zh: 他一连四天卧病在床。

sunset.definition:
n. the time in the evening at which the sun begins to fall below the horizon
n. atmospheric phenomena accompanying the daily disappearance of the sun
n. the daily event of the sun sinking below the horizon
s. of a declining industry or technology

examples.en: Even after sunset there was little moderation in the temperature.
examples.zh: 甚至在日落之后，气温也不见降低。

examples.en: We could see the sunset from the window.
examples.zh: 我们能从窗户看到日落。

examples.en: Never did I see such a beautiful sunset.
examples.zh: 我从没看过一个那么漂亮的日落。

superiority.definition: n. the quality of being superior\nn. the quality of being at a competitive advantage\nn. displaying a sense of being better than others
superiority.translation: n. 优越, 高傲\n[化] 优越性

examples.en: He said this with his typical air of superiority.
Is the idea of male superiority still common today?
The natural superiority of all Capricorns shouldn't be doubted any more.

sadly.definition: r. in an unfortunate way\nr. with sadness; in a sad manner
sadly.translation: adv. 悲痛地, 悲惨地, 悲伤地, 说来遗憾

examples.en: Sadly, I have to wake up early every day.
examples.zh: 不幸的是，我必须每天早起。

examples.en: "He used to love me," she answered sadly.
examples.zh: 他以前爱我，她伤心地回答。

examples.en: Sadly, most young people speak dialect only rarely.
examples.zh: 不幸的是，大多数年轻人都不常说方言了。

sadness.definition: n. emotions experienced when not in a state of well-being\nn. the state of being sad

examples.en: This shows that happiness and sadness are only separated by attitude.
examples.zh: 这表明幸福和悲痛之间只隔着看法。

examples.en: Do you know what sadness feels like?
examples.zh: 你知道悲伤的滋味么？

examples.en: Her eyes were full of sadness.
examples.zh: 她的眼神里充满了悲哀。

safely.definition: r. with safety; in a safe manner
safely.translation: adv. 安全地, 确实地

examples.en: The fishing boat which had been missing returned safely to port.
examples.zh: 消失了的渔船安全地回了港。

examples.en: It may safely be said that he will never succeed in business.
examples.zh: 我可以肯定的说，他做生意一定永远不会成功。

examples.en: The fishing boat that had been missing returned to its port safely.
examples.zh: 消失了的渔船安全地回了港。

sailor.definition: n. any member of a ship's crew
sailor.translation: n. 水手, 船员, 海员\n[法] 水手, 船员, 海员

examples.en: A sailor is at sea much of the time.
A sailor saw his fellow sailor sink from exhaustion.
As is usual with a sailor, he likes liquor very much.

salad.definition: n. food mixtures either arranged on a plate or tossed and served with a moist dressing; usually consisting of or including greens

examples.en: My mom forgot to add salt to the salad.
examples.zh: 我妈妈忘了往沙拉里加盐了。

examples.en: My mother forgot to add salt to the salad.
examples.zh: 我妈妈忘了往沙拉里加盐了。

examples.en: You have the choice of soup or salad.
examples.zh: 你有两种选择，汤，或沙拉。

sale.definition:
n. a particular instance of selling
n. the general activity of selling
n. an occasion (usually brief) for buying at specially reduced prices
n. the state of being purchasable; offered or exhibited for selling
sale.translation: n. 出售, 卖, 拍卖, 销售额, 廉价出售\n[经] 卖, 出售; 销售(货)

examples.en: The bargain sale will run for three days, beginning today.
examples.zh: 这场减价活动会持续三天，从今天开始。

examples.en: The sale prices are written in red ink.
examples.zh: 售价用红墨水写。

examples.en: Yanni held a big yard sale on Thursday.
examples.zh: 雅妮在周四举行了一场大型庭院旧货甩卖。

salesman.translation: n. 售货员, 推销员\n[经] 售货员, 店员, 推销员

examples.en: The customer and the salesman spoke for two hours on the phone.
examples.zh: 客人和售货员打了2小时电话。

examples.en: He makes a living as a salesman.
examples.zh: 他当推销员为生。

examples.en: I was mistaken for a salesman.
examples.zh: 我被误认为是推销员。

salt.definition:
n. a compound formed by replacing hydrogen in an acid by a metal (or a radical that acts like a metal)
n. white crystalline form of especially sodium chloride used to season and preserve food
n. the taste experience when common salt is taken into the mouth
v. add salt to
salt.translation: n. 盐, 风趣, 刺激\na. 含盐的, 咸的, 风趣的, 辛辣的\nvt. 加盐于, 用盐腌

examples.en: My mom forgot to add salt to the salad.
examples.zh: 我妈妈忘了往沙拉里加盐了。

examples.en: My mother forgot to add salt to the salad.
examples.zh: 我妈妈忘了往沙拉里加盐了。

examples.en: She discovered that she had run out of salt.
examples.zh: 她发现她已经断盐了。

sandwich.definition: n. two (or more) slices of bread with a filling between them\nv. make into a sandwich\nv. insert or squeeze tightly between two people or objects
sandwich.translation: n. 三明治, 夹心面包, 夹层板\nvt. 插入, 夹入, 把...制成三明治

examples.en: In my sandwich there is meat, cheese and tomatoes.
examples.zh: 我的三明治里有肉，奶酪和番茄。

examples.en: Tom said he saw Mary eating a sandwich in the park.
examples.zh: 汤姆说他看到玛丽在公园吃三文治。

examples.en: I think you should eat a ham sandwich.
examples.zh: 我认为你该吃火腿三明治。

sandy.definition: s of hair color; pale yellowish to yellowish brown\na resembling or containing or abounding in sand; or growing in sandy areas
sandy.translation: a. 沙的, 沙地的, 多沙的

examples.en: Tom sat down next to Mary on the sandy beach.
Sandy Jones isn't Sandy Lee, as why people have surnames.
Sandy goes out to get his shopping every afternoon.

sardine.definition: n. small fatty fish usually canned\nn. any of various small edible herring or related food fishes frequently canned

examples.en: I really need to fix my sardine net.
They were crammed in there like sardines in a can.
Passengers are packed in like sardines on city buses.
I hope the new plan will work out satisfactorily.
Everything came out satisfactorily through your good offices.
All the tasks have been fulfilled satisfactorily.

saturation.definition: n. the act of soaking thoroughly with a liquid\nn. a condition in which a quantity no longer responds to some external influence\nn. chromatic purity: freedom from dilution with white and hence vivid in hue
saturation.translation: n. 饱和, 渗透, 浸透, 色饱和度\n[计] 饱和度

examples.en: You can manually adjust the saturation of your image in this program.
Tom is a saturation diver.
The pulse ox sensor couldn't get a good oxygen saturation reading because Tom's hands were so cold.

saucer.definition: n. a small shallow dish for holding a cup at the table
saucer.translation: n. 茶碟, 茶托\n[医] 碟

examples.en: Tom poured some milk into a saucer for his cat.
Tom set down the bone china teacup into its saucer.
Kneeling, the doctor drank the tea out of the saucer.

sausage.definition: n. highly seasoned minced meat stuffed in casings

examples.en: Have you ever seen sausage being made?
examples.zh: 你见过灌肠的做法吗？

examples.en: Would you like bacon or sausage?
examples.zh: 你要培根还是要香肠?

examples.en: I often go to Chongqing to eat sausages.
examples.zh: 我经常去重庆吃香肠

saving.translation: n. 存款, 挽救, 节约\na. 搭救的, 节约的, 保留的, 补偿的\nprep. 除...之外

examples.en: I am saving money in order to study abroad.
examples.zh: 我正存钱出国留学。

examples.en: If you want security in your old age, begin saving now.
examples.zh: 如果你想安享晚年，现在就要开始储蓄了。

examples.en: They are saving their money for the purchase of a house.
examples.zh: 他们在储钱买房子。

saw.definition: n. hand tool having a toothed blade for cutting\nv. cut with a saw
saw.translation:
n. 锯子, 谚语
vt. 锯, 锯开, 来回移动
vi. 拉锯, 移动
see的过去式

examples.en: We saw a lot of live fish in the pond.
examples.zh: 我们看见池里有很多活鱼。

examples.en: I saw him at the station a few days ago.
examples.zh: 几天前我在站看到了他。

examples.en: Flavio saw a road with a car parked on it.
examples.zh: 弗拉维奥看到一条路，路上停著一辆车。

scarf.definition:
n. a garment worn around the head or neck or shoulders for warmth or decoration
v. masturbate while strangling oneself
v. unite by a scarf joint
v. wrap in or adorn with a scarf
scarf.translation: n. 围巾, 头巾, 领带, 领巾, 嵌接\nvt. 用围巾围, 嵌接

examples.en: Tom tried to convince Mary to knit him a scarf.
examples.zh: 汤姆想说服玛丽给他织一条围巾。

examples.en: The girl had a long scarf around her neck.
examples.zh: 女孩的脖子上围著一条长长的围巾。

examples.en: Vanessa loves to knit hats, scarves, and mittens in rainbow colors.
examples.zh: Vanessa喜欢针织彩虹色的帽子、围巾和连指手套。

scarlet.definition: n. a variable color that is vivid red but sometimes with an orange tinge
scarlet.translation: n. 猩红色, 绯红色, 红衣\na. 绯红色的, 鲜红色的

examples.en: Their faces looked inhuman, covered with scarlet and black paint.
Scarlet is a beautiful color, but I like fuchsia.
The petals were scarlet with streaks of gold.

sceptical.definition: s marked by or given to doubt\ns denying or questioning the tenets of especially a religion
sceptical.translation: a. 怀疑论的, 怀疑的

examples.en: Seeing the sceptical look on the girl's face, he fell silent.
People are often quite sceptical about things unless given credible evidence.
She can't help but be sceptical of him.

scientist.definition: n. a person with advanced knowledge of one or more sciences
scientist.translation: n. 科学家\n[医] 科学家

examples.en: It is not good for a scientist to get emotional.
examples.zh: 对一个科学家来说，多愁善感是不好的。

examples.en: He is proud that his father was a great scientist.
examples.zh: 他很自豪他父亲是个伟大的科学家。

examples.en: A true scientist would not approach the question this way.
examples.zh: 真正的科学家不会这样去思考。

scoff.translation: n. 嘲笑, 愚弄, 笑柄, 食品\nv. 嘲笑, 嘲弄, 贪吃, 狼吞虎咽地吃

examples.en: She scoffed at my poem.
